title: Rajesh Sharma reveals real reason behind hospitalisation on Prabhas' Fauzi set, dismisses earlier claims
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

In July this year, star Sudipa Chatterjee issued a press note revealing that star Rajesh Sharma had been hospitalised after as per reports suffering an insect bite on the set of Prabhas ’ soon-to-release movie Fauzi. However, in a recent interview with NDTV, Rajesh has now shared a health update and dismissed reports that an insect bite led to his hospitalisation.

Adding to this, Star Rajesh Sharma reveals diabetes led to severe infection. Rajesh Sharma reveals reason behind hospitalisation Rajesh revealed what actually happened and shared that he had been dealing with a skin problem in his right leg for a long time. His condition worsened as his diabetes levels were high, although he initially did not realise how serious the situation was. He added that his treatment is now over and that he is recovering, with hopes of returning to work within a week.

Meanwhile, Dismissing reports of an insect bite, he shared, "It's false news. Nothing happened on Prabhas's movie set. Neither Prabhas nor the unit was responsible in any way. They are nice people. Nothing happened in Hyderabad while I was shooting there. After I flew back to Kolkata, in a day or two, the situation became severe. Because my diabetes was very high and I didn't take it seriously at the beginning."

Notably, He further defended Sudipa and shared, "I have had a skin problem in my right leg for long. From there, I have got the infection. She's a good friend. Out of concern, she posted that. But she was wrong informed."

As per the latest buzz, Sudipa posted on Instagram and shared a statement on behalf of Rajesh’s family, which read, "Star Rajesh Sharma as per reports suffered an insect bite-possibly from a bug or a poisonous spider-while shooting at Ramoji Movie City for a movie starring renowned star Prabhas. After pack-up, Rajesh was chatting with local technicians in an area surrounded by dense vegetation when he felt an insect bite. As it did not seem serious at the time, he continued without seeking immediate medical attention.”

In further updates, "But six hours later, the star began experiencing severe pain in his right leg and felt unwell. “Despite his worsening condition, he boarded a flight back to Kolkata. During the journey, he developed a high fever, became increasingly restless, and his health deteriorated further. The following day, he was admitted to Manipal Hospital, Dhakuria. More than a day has passed since his hospitalisation but he suffers from high fever, breathlessness and a progressing infection in his right leg." the note further read.

On top of that, Prabhas is currently shooting for Hanu Raghavapudi’s Fauzi and Sandeep Reddy Vanga’s Spirit. Meanwhile, Rajesh is awaiting the rollout of his soon-to-release movie, Haiwaan. Helmed by Priyadarshan, the movie also stars Saif Ali Khan, Akshay Kumar and Saiyami Kher in key roles. It is scheduled to rollout in theatres on September 11.

title: ‘Can't accept Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama’: Ramanand Sagar's grandson Shiv Sagar says ‘fresh face’ was needed in Ramayana
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Ever since he was revealed as Lord Rama in Nitesh Tiwari's soon-to-release Ramayana adaptation, Ranbir Kapoor has divided fan opinions. After the rollout of the teaser and first look, many viewers were convinced he was the right choice, but others remained sceptical. Now, Shiv Sagar, grandson of Ramanand Sagar, who made the most memorable adaptation of the epic, has shared that Ranbir will bring baggage from his past roles into the movie.

Adding to this, Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama in Ramayana Part 1. ‘Can't accept Ranbir Kapoor as Rama’ Shiv Sagar is the grandson of legendary filmmaker Ramanand Sagar, who famously made the 1987 Doordarshan show Ramayan, and its follow-up, Lav-Kush. Of late, Shiv expressed his displeasure with the casting of Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, particularly after Ranbir had played a violent man in Animal.

Meanwhile, “Except for that one casting, I like the rest of the casting very much. Personally, I cannot accept Ranbir Kapoor as Ram because after Animal, I cannot accept him as Ram. When I look at Ram ji, I feel that a fresh face should have been taken,” Shiv Sagar shared, as per ANI.

Notably, “We have seen Ranbir in different roles; he is a very good star. Personally, I don't have anything against him. I think they must have taken him for the project because they want a marketing push, and maybe if they didn't take Ranbir, the movie wouldn't have been marketed so well, so that's also something to think about, but I personally believe that for such characters, it's better to take a new face,” he elaborated.

As per the latest buzz, The director-producer lauded the rest of the cast, including Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. “You can take a very strong supporting cast, like Yash is looking very good, Sai Pallavi is looking very good, they don't have that much baggage. He has a lot of baggage. That's why we usually take a new face in our serials, so they don't have any baggage or history,” shared Shiv Sagar. However, the filmmaker conceded that, in the end, his personal opinion will not matter if the audience accepts Ranbir in the role. He shared that ‘the public is the king’ and they will have the final word on the matter once the movie is rolled out.

In further updates, Directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, the soon-to-release Ramayana is a two-part movie starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash, Ravie Dubey, and Sunny Deol in lead roles. title: Aashiqui star Rahul Roy reveals dancing at weddings for ₹2 lakh to earn after brain stroke: ‘Getting work was difficult’
body: Here's the latest relationship update doing the rounds:

Of late, Bollywood star Rahul Roy found himself back in the spotlight after videos of him dancing at weddings and performing to his old songs went widely shared on social media. Now, in an interview with the Times of India, Rahul opened up about his financial struggles and opened up that he has been performing at weddings and events to keep things going as he rebuilds his life after a brain stroke.

Adding to this, Rahul Roy opens up about financial struggles. Rahul Roy on building his life from scratch, facing financial struggles The star opened up that he has been fighting a ₹ 30 lakh legal case for years and that he and his brother are working to settle it. Rahul also opened up that a few years ago, he went through a divorce case during which he transferred his assets to his wife. He shared that he is now trying to rebuild his life and career and create his empire from scratch.

Meanwhile, Rahul added, "The last five years have almost been like a break because I was recuperating. There was no work. If that hadn’t happened, I would have done much more. But now, I am getting some work and want to do a lot more. I was happy to be back on the set and face the camera. I am really thankful to the people who are trusting me. In my 37-year journey in films, I believe I have done some good work, and now I am looking forward to doing more.”

Notably, Talking about his financial struggles, Rahul shared, "I have expenses, and I need the money. Getting work after my brain stroke in 2020 was difficult. It’s been five years since then, and I was doing whatever I could to keep things going. Sometimes, I earn ₹ 2 lakh or 4 lakh by dancing at weddings. People who troll me don’t know that this is hard work. I have to earn my bread and butter too.”

As per the latest buzz, In November 2020, Rahul suffered a cerebrovascular stroke while he was in Kargil for the shoot of LAC – Live The Battle. He was rushed to Srinagar for treatment and was subsequently shifted to Mumbai. The star was admitted to Nanavati Hospital, where he spent several days in the ICU.

In further updates, His journey in Bollywood began with Aashiqui in 1990, which saw him share the screen with Anu Aggarwal. The movie became a massive hit and changed Rahul’s career overnight, making him a popular face among Hindi movie audiences. After a spate of flops in the 90s, Rahul moved to television in the 2000s. In 2007, he participated in the first season of Bigg Boss and emerged as the winner, defeating Carol Gracias and receiving the ₹ 1 crore rupees prize.

title: Akshay Kumar recalls house help spilling 4 glasses of water on Amitabh Bachchan: ‘What will happen now?’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bollywood legend Amitabh Bachchan rose to stardom after his 1973 movie Zanjeer broke ticket-window records and established him as a star. Over the decades, the star has amassed a massive fan following across generations and walks of life. The star still greets a sea of followers who wait for his glimpse outside his bungalow in Mumbai every Sunday. Of late, Akshay Kumar shared an anecdote that offered a glimpse into Amitabh's immense stardom.

Adding to this, Akshay Kumar shared a hilarious anecdote about Amitabh Bachchan on KBC. Akshay Kumar's house help spilled water on Amitabh Bachchan Akshay appeared on Kaun Banega Crorepati with Saif Ali Khan. The two stars were present on the show to promote their soon-to-release movie Haiwaan. During a segment of the show, Akshay recalled the time Amitabh Bachchan visited his house when he lived in Lokhandwala, Mumbai.

Meanwhile, Akshay opened up that one of the people who worked at his house was such a huge fan of Amitabh that he became overwhelmed upon seeing the superstar in person. In his excitement, he ended up spilling glasses of water on the star.

Notably, Addressing Amitabh, Akshay shared, “Sir, do you remember when you came to my house? I am talking about Lokhandwala, when I used to live there. The person who worked at my house had to give you some water. There were three or four glasses kept there. I remember it very clearly. Sir was wearing a kurta and that boy was from Allahabad. He looked at you and simply couldn't believe that he was actually giving Amitabh ji a glass of water."

As per the latest buzz, He added, "So, he came over with the water. There were four glasses, and he ended up spilling all four glasses on your kurta because he was so stunned that he couldn't even see properly. I was thinking, what will happen now? Sir is obviously very tall, so I had to give you my kurta so that it would fit you."
In further updates, The anecdote left Amitabh and those present laughing on the show.

On top of that, Haiwaan is a crime thriller movie co-written and directed by Priyadarshan. It is a remake of Priyadarshan's own 2016 Malayalam movie Oppam and stars Akshay Kumar, Saif Ali Khan, Boman Irani, Shriya Pilgaonkar and Saiyami Kher. Mohanlal also makes a cameo appearance in the movie. The movie also marks the final on-screen performance of late legendary star Asrani, who passed away in October 2025.
The movie stars Saif Ali Khan as a blind character, Vibijeet Khurana, while Akshay plays the negative role of Abhijeet.

title: 'Orwellian dystopia': Allahabad HC reprimands Noida DM over DU student's NSA detention during Noida workers protest
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:
Allahabad High Court came down heavily on Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam last week while quashing the detention of a Delhi University student and called her conduct “despotic”.

Adding to this, Akriti Chaudhary was detained under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) and the order of detention was passed by Noida DM Medha Roopam. (X/@MedhaRoopam) On Wednesday last week, the Allahabad high court quashed the detention order against a 25-year-old Delhi University graduate Akriti Chaudhary who has been in judicial custody for around five months in connection with the Noida workers’ protest of April 2026, saying her detention was based on a “concocted story”.
Meanwhile, Chaudhary was detained under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) and the order of detention was passed by Roopam.

Notably, While quashing the move, the bench of justice Atul Sreedharan and justice Achal Sachdev made a reference to English writer George Orwell, who is well-known for his dystopian novel ‘1984’ and his allegorical novella ‘Animal Farm’.
As per the latest buzz, The court shared that “it shan't be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia”, reported Live Law.
In further updates, It also shared that when bureaucrats and cops go against their oath, they may be viewed as an “oppressive vestige of the British Empire”.

On top of that, The bench also ordered immediate rollout of Chaudhary and awarded her a compensation of ₹ 5 lakh and directed that it must be recovered from the salaries of the district magistrate to every officer responsible “right down to the SHO”.

The court observed that the police report only contained allegations against Chaudhary and it was on the district magistrate to examine the record 'threadbare' and see if the case warranted stringent action such as the NSA.

title: Aviation firm files ₹3 crore defamation suit against Nora Fatehi for ‘toy plane’ remark
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

An aviation company has filed a ₹ 3 crore rupees civil defamation suit against Bollywood star Nora Fatehi at a Gandhinagar court, alleging her "derogatory and reckless" comments on social media calling its chartered aircraft a "Lego airplane" severely damaged its reputation.
Adding to this, Nora Fatehi has landed in row for her remarks. About the defamation suit The court of senior civil judge R Agarwal will hear the matter on September 25.

Meanwhile, According to the suit filed by Dunes Aviation, Nora recorded videos inside a Cessna Citation CJ2 aircraft during a Mumbai-Jaipur flight in December last year, describing the aircraft as a "miniature", a "toy" and a "Lego airplane" and posted them on her Instagram handle.
Notably, The company alleged that "reckless" statements made by the star, who has more than 4.6 crore rupees followers, triggered booking cancellations and severely hurt its commercial operations.

As per the latest buzz, The suit, filed in April this year, shared that Nora Fatehi's statements were "reckless, irresponsible, and made without any technical knowledge, verification or factual basis".

In further updates, Dunes Aviation shared that owing to Nora Fatehi's substantial follower base, her "reckless statements" have caused "serious reputational damage, loss of goodwill and adverse commercial impact" to the company.
On top of that, The company has suffered a 15-20 per cent drop in bookings and a rise in cancellations.
It shared the aircraft was standard and ideally sized for the journey undertaken by the defendant, is fully DGCA-certified, airworthy and lawfully operated under a valid NSOP.

It had a bumper opening and proved to be unstoppable on the first weekend. Let's take a look at how the movie performed on its first Monday.

Adding to this, Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window earnings day 4: The drama stars Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, and Shweta Tripathi. Has Mirzapur passed the Monday test? For a movie without a superstar at its centre, the numbers so far have been amazing at the ticket-window. Ahead of rollout, most trade experts estimated an opening of ₹ 18-20 crore rupees for the movie. But Mirzapur defied those expectations and managed to collected ₹ 25.75 crore rupees. This means that Mirzapur The Movie has officially crossed the ₹ 100 crore rupees net mark in India! Its total collection stands at ₹ 109.25 crore rupees .

Directed by Hardik Gajjar, the movie rolled out on May 7, 2026, and stars Siddharth Gupta (Lord Krishna), Sanskruti Jayana (Satyabhama), Sushmita Bhat (Radha), Nivaashiyni Krishnan (Rukmini), alongside Jackie Shroff and Ashutosh Rana. Inspired by the Brahma Vaivarta Purana by Vyasa, the story follows Lord Krishna’s journey from Vrindavan to Dwarka and Kurukshetra while exploring themes of divine love, devotion and emotional connection.
Notably, World Forum For Art and Culture (WFCA) and Raj Kurup's Creativelands have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Shankar who will be guiding the team further.

As per the latest buzz, "Krishna means the most attractive self. It is the divinity that is the most attractive; the energy that pulls everything to it. When you realise your life and the whole world is just a Leela (play), then Krishna is born inside you," Shankar shared in a note.

In further updates, Producer Sajan Raj Kurup added, "With the blessings of Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, who has nurtured the entire world with his grace and transformed the lives of millions, this movie finds its best place at the feet of Gurudev."

On top of that, For Siddharth, the audience response goes far beyond just numbers at the ticket-window. “More than that, it’s a win for the people who believe in what we are propagating: our history and our message. Personally, we are incredibly happy that our performances are being applauded. When you watch the ticket-window numbers grow, no matter how modest the starting point was on Day 1, it’s a crazy feeling. Honestly, it has nothing to do with us at this point—it’s entirely being guided by Lord Krishna.”

Combining the rigorous vocal heritage of her Hindustani classical training under the Agra Gharana with a sharp, modern pop sensibility, Bagchi’s two-hour live setlist promises to be a masterclass in sonic contrast. Followers can expect heavy-hitting live renditions of her career-defining catalog, including the cinematic ‘ Nazariya Ki Maari ’ (Heeramandi), the high-octane Pan-Indian banger ‘ Peelings ’ ( Pushpa 2: The Rule - Hindi), her chart-topping pop collaborations, and the dance-floor staple ‘ Barbaadiyan ’ (Shiddat), alongside the intimate indie-pop streaming favorite ‘ Ishq Hai ’ (Mismatched).

Meanwhile, Built entirely on an ‘anti-widely shared’ strategy of artistic integrity, the tour honours the audience's time with a strict, 100% authentic ‘no lip-sync’ live guarantee backed by a massive orchestral band. It also carries deep personal significance as a three-generation family tribute, fulfilling her late grandfather's unreleased dream of seeing a professional musician rise from their lineage.

Notably, Madhubanti Bagchi shared, “Performing live is where music truly comes alive for me, and this debut tour is the culmination of everything I’ve worked toward. For years, people have connected with my voice through movie screens and streaming playlists, but ‘This Is Who We Are’ is about breaking down that digital wall. I’ve waited a long time to look my followers in the eye and share this energy with them and it’s going to be an unforgettable, completely live celebration.”

As per the latest buzz, Abhinav Kumar Upadhyay, Managing Director, Perfect Harmony Productions shared, “Madhubanti Bagchi represents a rare, generational shift in the live music landscape. Over the last 25 years, our mission has always been to elevate pure musical excellence. Her ability to anchor a massive commercial production while maintaining the soul of classical fusion is exactly what live audiences have been craving. This tour isn't just a series of concerts; it’s a high-production celebration of where Indian music is heading.”

In further updates, In a bid to foster true inclusivity and deep community engagement, the tour will eliminate VIP seating, ensuring every attendee enjoys an equal experience, with special student category passes starting at an accessible Rs. 499.

title: Delhi HC rejects Swatantra Bhardwaj’s habeas corpus plea in CJP protest assault case
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Delhi high court on Monday dismissed a habeas corpus petition filed by right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj, who was detained in connection with an assault case registered under the SC/ST Act. Bhardwaj allegedly severely injured a 38-year-old man during a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest against NEET-UG irregularities at Jantar Mantar in June.

Adding to this, Bhardwaj was produced before duty magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court through video conference by the Delhi police. (Instagram/ bhardwaj_swatantra_official) “The petition is dismissed,” a bench of justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja shared.

Meanwhile, This was after Bhardwaj’s lawyer Umesh Sharma submitted that his arrest was illegal since he was arrested in connection with a first information report which was quashed by the Supreme Court on September 1.

Notably, To be sure, the Supreme Court on September 1 quashed FIRs registered across the country in connection with the CJP-led protests in July, invoking its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, even as the group withdrew its call for a September 5 march in Delhi following assurances from the Centre that it would honour its commitments to withdraw criminal cases and compensation to families of students who died by suicide.

As per the latest buzz, The top court ordered that all FIRs relating to the protests between July 20 and 25 in the states and Union territories, including those not formally brought before it, would not be pursued or investigated and would be treated as closed for all purposes. It also directed that similar FIRs pending in other states and Union territories be treated in the same manner.

In further updates, However, Delhi police counsel Sanjay Lau submitted that the FIR in connection with which Bhardwaj was detained had not been quashed by the Supreme Court on September 1. He shared Bhardwaj was remanded to one-day judicial custody on Sunday and was produced before the trial court through video conferencing again on Monday, following which he was sent to 14 days of judicial custody. Lau argued that there was no question of illegal detention as Bhardwaj’s custody was pursuant to orders passed by the trial court.
On top of that, Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr on Friday , hours after the CJP held a protest outside the Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault.

Bhardwaj was produced before duty magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court through video conference by the Delhi police. The detention came amid outrage over an interview in which Bhardwaj claimed he had “cracked the skull” of the student activist’s father during the June 23 protest and escaped arrest because of his political connections.

title: Bipasha Basu says she ‘started the trend’ of muscular women in Bollywood: ‘It's not just about looking good'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Earlier, Mrunal Thakur's old video went widely shared in which she was seemingly mocking Bipasha Basu's physique and how muscular she is. The clip started a debate about women's health, and Mrunal faced a lot of trolling regarding the same. Now, Bipasha has opened up about starting the trend of female stars looking muscular.

Adding to this, Bipasha Basu spoke starting the trend of female stars looking muscular. (File Photo/ PTI) Bipasha Basu on muscular women in Bollywood In conversation with Elle India, Bipasha admitted that in the beginning of the 2000s, female actors used to be very petite, fair, with very delicate features. Among them, she stood out differently as she was tall with a very athletic build and tanned complexion.

Meanwhile, She also admitted that muscular women weren't accepted in Bollywood, but she started the trend. She shared, “I don’t think women with more muscle tone were very acceptable as actresses. But I think I started the trend, and I started preaching ‘love yourself’ to everyone because I realised it’s not just about looking good. It’s more intrinsic. You need to be healthy.”

Notably, Bipasha shared that the trend she started led many women to exercise and focus on being healthy. This led to everybody understanding the benefits of exercising. However, Bipasha doubts whether people are doing it for the right reasons or just to look good physically.

As per the latest buzz, In the same interaction, Bipasha spoke about the pressure of ageing. She shared, “Ageing is like the biggest sin that you can commit. I believe that I like myself more, the person that I am today, much more than what I used to be in my twenties. What other people are doing, it’s their call. I don’t judge that. But for me, I’m never going to fall into the pressure of wanting to look younger than what I am. I’m very happy with the way I am growing older, and I’m very proud of my age.”

In further updates, In an old interview, when Mrunal was still starring in TV shows, the star was seen speaking with her Kumkum Bhagya co-star Arjit Taneja. During their conversation, the two were discussing the kind of physique one might prefer in a partner. Mrunal referred to Bipasha while responding to Arjit and shared, “Do you want to marry a girl who is manly with muscles? Go marry Bipasha. Listen, I am far better than Bipasha, ok."
On top of that, Mrunal faced backlash after her old comment went widely shared, and the star later apologised for the same on social media.

title: Sajid Nadiadwala’s production house Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment leases Andheri office for Rs 2.46 crores
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

The lease commenced on August 1, 2026, while the agreement was registered on September 1, 2026. As per the documents, the initial monthly licence fee for the two office units has been fixed at Rs 8,26,875. The transaction also includes a security deposit of Rs 30 lakhs. The registered documents do not mention the total area of the leased premises.

Adding to this, The offices are located on the eighth floor of Lotus Grandeur, a commercial building in Andheri West. The premises also come with two car parking spaces. Andheri West, particularly the Veera Desai Road area, is known for its mix of corporate offices, production houses, creative businesses and residential developments.

Meanwhile, Under the terms of the agreement, the monthly rent will increase by 5% every 12 months. Following the first escalation, the rent will rise to approximately Rs 8.68 lakhs from the 13th month. For the final four months of the 28-month lease period, the monthly rent will increase further to around Rs 9.12 lakhs.

Notably, Taking the agreed rent escalation into account, the documents indicate that the total rent payable throughout the 28-month tenure will be approximately Rs 2.46 crores. The agreement also carries a 12-month lock-in period, requiring the premises to remain under the agreed occupancy commitment during the first year.
As per the latest buzz, Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment Private Limited and Rhea and Dia Enterprises Pvt Ltd could not be reached for comment regarding the transaction.
In further updates, Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment’s Previous Property Deals

On top of that, This is not the first major real estate transaction involving Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment. In October 2025, the production house purchased two apartments in Mumbai’s Prabhadevi for Rs 36.57 crores, according to property registration documents reviewed by Square Yards.

One of the transactions involved an apartment at Hubtown Twenty Five North. The 2,390 sq ft apartment, along with an additional 208 sq ft area, was purchased for Rs 18.57 crores. Located on the 23rd floor, the property also came with two car parking spaces.

body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

The collaboration was formalised on Janmashtami in the presence of Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Founder of The Art of Living. As part of the association, an MoU has been signed under which Gurudev will guide the team on the movie's global presentation and the development of the larger trilogy.

Adding to this, The immediate focus of the collaboration will be to take Krishnavataram: Part 1 - Hridayam to international audiences through a wider theatrical rollout. The movie is planned to reach Indian diaspora communities and audiences across different markets in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and English.

Meanwhile, Speaking about the movie's vision, Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar shared, “Krishna means the most attractive the Self. It is the divinity that is the most attractive; the energy that pulls everything to it. When you realize your life and the whole world is just a Leela (play), then Krishna is born inside you".
Notably, Producer Dr. Sajan Raj Kurup shared the collaboration would help the team take the story and its cultural themes to audiences outside India.

As per the latest buzz, “With the blessings of Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, who has nurtured the entire world with his grace and transformed the lives of millions, this movie finds its best place at the feet of Gurudev. With Krishnavataram, we take pride in taking every bit of Indian culture to the world and presenting our cultural beliefs, which are a fundamental part of our very existence. Our vision is to build Krishnavataram into a global cultural movement that celebrates cinema, art, and legacy,” he shared.

In further updates, According to the makers, the collaboration is also expected to explore formats beyond the theatrical movie, including series, music, live experiences, games, education and other cultural initiatives.

On top of that, WFAC was founded in September 2020 under The Art of Living with the aim of bringing together artists, performers and art enthusiasts from around the world. The organisation works around Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar's vision of “One World Family” and the principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.

The association with Creativeland Studios is expected to provide a platform for exploring Krishna's story through different forms of contemporary cultural and artistic expression while retaining its roots in Indian traditions.

title: Babita Singh Reporting shows how the most dangerous form of patriarchy exists disguised as 'concern'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

I started watching Babita Singh Reporting , the new Nimisha Sajayan movie, expecting a murder mystery. What I was met with was a striking coming-of-age story that deals with identity, gender roles, and subtle patriarchy. And while there have been many movies dealing with these themes, what set this gem apart from Ambiecka Pandit was how it portrayed women being put in boxes without villainising anyone. The men exist around these women, thinking they protect the women. But all they are protecting is the status quo. And that is the most dangerous form of patriarchy, one that puts women down in the name of love and concern.

Adding to this, Babita Singh Reporting stars Nimisha Sajayan in the titular role. Patriarchy that is not malicious Babita Singh Reporting is about the titular police officer, who hardly has the confidence to call herself one. Sandwiched between her official duty and familial responsibilities, Babita, aka Baby, has never really tried to find out what she can do. It doesn’t help that she is always belittled by her family and in-laws. When they are all out having ice-creams, they select a sugar-free one for her. After all, she should watch her weight. She is told she doesn’t need the ‘headache’ of the job. None of this is malicious. It is out of genuine, yet misplaced concern.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by What Makes A Cinema (@whatmakesacinema)

Notably, In a striking scene, her husband is distraught about the state his life is in, and he casually brings up how he had rishtas from Brahmin women, but still ‘chose’ Baby, a woman from a different caste with a different mother tongue. It is supposed to be a magnanimous gesture in his eyes, but one that makes Babita feel this small in an instant. Mind you, the movie never portrays Babita’s family, in-laws, or husband as bad or evil. They are, for the lack of a better term, casual sexists, conditioned to believe that their patriarchal shackles are actually some protective armour for their women.

As per the latest buzz, Perhaps that is why the movie and its protagonist are finding resonance among viewers. Social media is full of reels saying this movie shows the ‘truth’ about society. The last time a Hindi movie inspired similar conversations was the Sanya Malhotra -starrer Mrs. But Babita Singh Reporting shows a tougher grind for the woman who is neither confident in her work nor at home, only due to conditioning. That has hit home.
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shweta Gupta (@reelflickss)

On top of that, “The first reaction was ‘I have met so many Babys in my life’,” was what Nimisha Sajayan had told us, talking about the movie prior to its rollout. She is a Malayali who grew up in Mumbai, while Babita is from Madhya Pradesh. But the cultural and linguistic divide doesn’t matter. the emotions are universal, the challenges are universal,” Nimisha added.

As director Ambiecka Pandit put it in a chat with us: “At the beginning of the movie, she is a wife, a daughter-in-law, and a cop. She is identified by the roles. She has forgotten who Babita is because she has suppressed it so much.”

title: Who is Surabhi Vanzara? Emraan Hashmi's Murder co-star roasted Samay Raina for ‘disturbing entire nation’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

India’s Got Latent 2 has brought attention to several participants on the show. Influencers such as Geni Kamki, Chello Meme and others have gone widely shared on social media after their appearances on the show, particularly for their interactions and exchanges with Samay Raina . The latest contestant to attract attention is star and stand-up comedian Surabhi Vanzara. Videos of her clapping back at Samay and other members of the panel have gone widely shared, bringing her back into the spotlight.

Adding to this, Surabhi Vanzara on India's Got Latent 2. Who is Surabhi Vanzara? Surabhi Vanzara is not a new face in the entertainment industry. She has been working in the industry for several years and has appeared across television, films and digital platforms. She began her career with television shows such as C.I.D., Aahat, Ssshhhh...Koi Hai and Hello Inspector, among others, where she appeared in episodic roles.

Meanwhile, Her major break came with the 2003 television show Jassi Jaisi Koi Nahin, in which she played the character of Maria. The show, starring Mona Singh, Apurva Agnihotri and Rakshanda Khan, became popular with television audiences and gave Surabhi another prominent role early in her career.

Notably, In 2004, Surabhi made an appearance in the Bollywood movie Murder, alongside Emraan Hashmi and Mallika Sherawat. Directed by Anurag Basu, the movie saw Surabhi play Radhika, a character connected to Emraan Hashmi’s Sunny and involved in the movie’s later developments.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by ααrαv. (@_aarav.edits)

In further updates, Rolled out in 2004, Murder became a major commercial success and is considered one of the films that helped establish Emraan Hashmi as a prominent star. The movie also received attention for its subject, music and performances by Emraan and Mallika.

On top of that, Surabhi later appeared in another Emraan Hashmi movie, Tumsa Nahin Dekha, although it did not perform as well at the ticket-window. She was also part of Hate Story 2. On television, she has appeared in shows including F.I.R., Hitler Didi and Qubool Hai.

title: 25 Years of Nayak: Anil Kapoor says, “The love for your country… Will never be irrelevant” in a heartfelt note
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Anil Kapoor marked 25 years of Nayak with a heartfelt note, reflecting on Shivaji Rao, the movie’s message and why its themes remain relevant.

Adding to this, In his post, Anil Kapoor wrote, “25 years of Nayak. What drew me to Shivaji Rao was never just the journey from a common man to the Chief Minister. It was what he chose to do once he got there, to use the power he had to make a difference to the people.”

Meanwhile, He further recalled the significance of portraying a character driven by a sense of purpose, adding, “To portray a role with that kind of purpose was a privilege and perhaps that is why Nayak continues to find its way back to people even after 25 years.”

Notably, The star also reflected on the movie's central message and why he continues to be proud of being associated with it. “The love for your country, and the desire to do better for its people will never be irrelevant, and I will always be proud to have been a part of such a story,” he wrote.

As per the latest buzz, Directed by S. Shankar, Nayak follows Shivaji Rao, a television cameraman and reporter played by Anil Kapoor. The story begins when Shivaji gets an opportunity to interview Maharashtra Chief Minister Balraj Chauhan, played by Amrish Puri.

In further updates, During the live interview, Shivaji questions the Chief Minister on issues concerning the state and puts him in a difficult position. In an attempt to counter the reporter's criticism, the Chief Minister challenges Shivaji to take charge as Chief Minister for a day and experience the pressures of running the state.

title: Gaiety-Galaxy shuts temporarily, owner says it’s a technical issue
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mumbai’s iconic Gaiety Galaxy or G7 as it is known hit a road block with no movie screenings on Monday . The complex has as per reports been temporarily shut down. On Monday, a post by a Netizen showed a notice outside the theatre from Bandra police, that shared that the cinema hall has been closed because the management did not renew its license.

Adding to this, Gaiety-Galaxy The theatre was playing shows regularly till Sunday but didn’t play any shows from Monday onwards. Owner Manoj Desai when contacted told HTCity, “The actual reason is some of the cables in the theatre got burned. We have to arrange for new cables from Lohar chawl, South Mumbai. Till that is arranged our shows cannot resume. It’s just a technical issue, nothing more than that.”
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by HT City (@htcity)
Notably, Gaiety-Galaxy was built on November 24, 1972. Filmmaker Ramesh Sippy’s movie Seeta Aur Geeta (1972) was the inaugural movie.

As per the latest buzz, G7 multiplex originally started with just 3 theatres – Gaiety, Galaxy and Gemini. Gaiety and Galaxy are the biggest screens, consisting of a stall and balcony. While Gaiety is the bigger one, comprising nearly 1000 seats, Galaxy has around 800 seats. Gemini with just one class, has around 240 seats.

title: Krystle D'Souza says she was offered Dhurandhar song Shararat 4 days before shoot: ‘I was very scared’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Krytle D'Souza talks about learning the dance steps for Dhurandhar track Shararat. What Krystle shared Krystle was the latest guest on Farah Khan's YouTube channel, and the two spoke about her recent win on The Traitors Season 2 and also her superhit song Shararat. When Farah asked how did she get the song, the star shared, “This is the first time I am doing an item song. Honestly when I got the call from Mukesh [Chhabra] Sir, I was sitting right there (inside her home, near the balcony) in my corner with my girlfriends. He shared we are shooting a song in 4 days and one girl is already selected. The team wants to see if you will be able to do it. I shared ok give me some time and I cut the call.”

Adding to this, Krystle added that she immediately asked her girlfriends whether she should do this song and they all screamed yes in unison. She told Farah that she is not a trained dancer and has only performed in some award shows. She also added that while she was shooting she had no idea that the movie would be such a huge success. “He did not even give me proper details, he just shared that it has big faces and it is a very big movie. Then I went for the rehearsals, where Vijay [Ganguly, choreographer] sir was there, and Aditya [Dhar, director] sir was also there… and they made us do some 11 different steps. That time the hook step was not final so we had 11 steps in mind and after that I was selected. I was very scared,” she added.

Meanwhile, Shararat is set during a wedding celebration in the Ranveer Singh -starrer, with the two actors portraying wedding dancers at a posh Karachi wedding. The song is composed by Sashwat Sachdev and sung by Madhubanti Bagchi and Jasmine Sandlas. Vijay Ganguly has choreographed the track.

Notably, Dhurandhar is a spy thriller starring Ranveer Singh in the lead, alongside Akshaye Khanna, Arjun Rampal, R. Madhavan, and Sanjay Dutt. The movie has been a massive success at the ticket-window, becoming India’s highest-grossing movie of 2025.

title: ‘Tameez mein rehna chahiye’: Kailash Kher addresses Samay Raina-Sharon Verma’s Kashmiri Pandit-Bihari row
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Kailash Kher has called for greater awareness and civility in public discourse, urging people to remain “chaitanye” (alert) and “tameez” (polite) amid criticism surrounding jokes involving Bihar and Kashmir on the stand-up comedy show India’s Got Latent .

Adding to this, Kailash Kher addressed Samay Raina and Sharon Verma's India's Got Latent row. In conversation with ANI, Kher was asked about comedians making fun of statements associated with Kashmiri Pandits and Biharis and about the broader debate around stand-up comedy on social media.

Meanwhile, “Look, if I'll tell you in terms of music, then music is not just a tune its something that can also make you laugh, its also a form of discipline. So, you should stay in music. If your music tune is not correct, then you may end in making fun of someone," he shared.

Notably, Kher then stressed the importance of conduct and politeness. He shared, “To islie manushye ko chaitanye mein rehna chahiye, tameez mein rehna chahiye… or apni apni tameez se sb baat krein, to sbko itna to pta hi hai kaise jeena hai, kese hasna hai or kese hsaana hai, kese kisi ka dil jeetna hai…(So, a person should be alert, should be polite, and should talk to everyone politely. Everyone knows how to live, how to laugh, how to win the hearts of people)."

As per the latest buzz, He also reflected on his own journey to fame, saying he had always tried to conduct himself politely. “I have always been polite,” he shared, while acknowledging that popularity can bring criticism, envy and hostility.

In further updates, Kailash Kher's remarks came amid criticism of an exchange between comedian Samay Raina and comedian Sharon Verma during Season 2 of 'India's Got Latent', which has attracted political attention over jokes involving Bihar and Kashmir.
On top of that, Sharon Verma, a former contestant from the first season, appeared as a panellist alongside Samay Raina, Orry, Archana Puran Singh and Nishant Suri.

During the episode, Raina made a joke about Verma's Bihari roots and stereotypes surrounding migration for work. Verma responded with a joke about Raina's Kashmiri identity and "getting stoned", and also shared she had "atleast left her state by choice."

title: Parineeti Chopra's web series debut Shaque: Trust No One to stream from September 24 on Netflix
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Created by Rensil D’Silva and Siddharth P. Malhotra, directed by Rensil D’Silva, and backed by Alchemy Films, Shaque: Trust No One explores the fragile line between trust and suspicion, instinct and truth, love and obsession. The ensemble is led by Parineeti Chopra, marking her series debut, as a mother in search of her missing child. But as answers finally begin to surface, a chilling question takes hold: can she trust the very people closest to her?

Adding to this, Tanya Bami, Series Head, Netflix India, shared, “Shaque is a gripping emotional crime drama with elements of a thriller but at its heart, it is a story about a mother’s relentless nine-year search for her child. The story effortlessly moves between the emotional intensity of a mother’s search and the tension of a tightly woven thriller. The characters are central to this journey, each carrying their own conflicts and secrets, constantly shifting our understanding of what has happened and where the truth lies. We’re thrilled to collaborate again with creator-producer Siddharth P. Malhotra and partner with Rensil D’Silva as he makes his Netflix debut with this story. With a powerhouse female ensemble featuring Parineeti Chopra, Jennifer Winget, Soni Razdan and Harleen Sethi, alongside Tahir Raj Bhasin, Sumeet Vyas and Anup Soni, Shaque promises to be a perfect binge-watch.”

Meanwhile, Thrilled for his fourth outing with Netflix, creator and producer Siddharth P. Malhotra shares, “When Rensil narrated the story to me, I was hooked. There was something about the world he had created that immediately stayed with me, and I knew I had to be a part of it – that this was a story that needed to be told. Being involved with Rensil as a co-creator and producer, alongside Sapna, has been an absolute pleasure. Shaque: Trust No One is relentless, nerve-wracking, emotional and incredibly pacey. It has everything I look for in a great thriller – a deeply emotional core, complex relationships, unexpected twists and the constant feeling that you are one step away from the truth. At its heart, the story begins with a mother searching for her missing child. But that search soon becomes something much bigger – a journey into the secrets and relationships of the people closest to her. What happens when the people you instinctively trust become the very people you begin to question? What makes Shaque particularly compelling is that beneath the mystery and suspense lies a deeply human story about motherhood, instinct and resilience. It explores that uncomfortable space where trust begins to break down and every relationship starts carrying a question. After Tribhanga, Maharaj and Ikka, I’m incredibly proud to bring Shaque: Trust No One to Netflix. I can’t wait for audiences to enter this world with us — and spend the journey guessing, questioning and wondering where the truth really lies.”

Notably, Director and co-creator Rensil D’Silva adds, “Shaque is a thriller built on uncertainty. Every revelation raises another question, and every relationship has another layer waiting to be uncovered. What fascinated me was the opportunity to tell a suspenseful story through the deeply emotional journey of a mother who has spent nine years refusing to give up. I've been fortunate to collaborate with Netflix on this bold, deeply emotional and layered story. We have tried to create a world where the audience is constantly second-guessing what they see and whom they trust. I hope Shaque keeps audiences guessing right until the very end.”

As per the latest buzz, Joining Chopra are Soni Razdan, Anup Soni, Jennifer Winget, Tahir Raj Bhasin, Harleen Sethi, Dhruv Chowdhary, and Sumeet Vyas, who feature in this stellar ensemble. Together, the cast inhabits a world where every relationship carries its own questions, and every revelation has the power to change what you thought you knew.
In further updates, Shaque: Trust No One premieres September 24, only on Netflix!

title: SCOOP: Karan Johar-Shanaya Kapoor’s Student Of The Year 3 gets a BOLD makeover; web series to be a Class-meets-Euphoria youth drama
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A source told Bollywood Hungama, “To begin with, while Student Of The Year (2012) and Student Of The Year 2 (2019) were films, the third installment of Student Of The Year will be a web series. Secondly, the first two parts were candyfloss and light-hearted entertainers. Student Of The Year 3, meanwhile, is in an altogether different space.”

Adding to this, The source explained, “Student Of The Year 3 is darker, edgier and far more intense than the previous two instalments. Tonally, it is being envisioned as a Class-meets-Euphoria kind of show — blending the privileged, high-pressure world of young students, complicated friendships and relationships seen in Netflix’s Indian series Class with the bold, provocative and emotionally turbulent treatment associated with the globally popular Euphoria. Viewers will be pleasantly surprised by the conflicts, relationships and overall genre of the third part. Moreover, this kind of youth-driven, edgy content has an audience across markets, which could further widen its appeal and viewership.”

Meanwhile, The source also shared, “Student Of The Year 3 is expected to rollout this year, on JioHotstar.” There were also reports that Student Of The Year 3 will be called Student Of The Year 3 – After The Dark but the source shared that it may or may not be the final title. The official announcement will give a clearer idea about the same.

Notably, Student Of The Year 3 is directed by Reema Maya. As per reports, Shanaya Kapoor will be seen in a double role. The first part marked the debut of Varun Dhawan, Alia Bhatt and Sidharth Malhotra, and was directed by Karan Johar. Student Of The Year 2 , on the other hand, starred Tiger Shroff and launched Ananya Panday and Tara Sutaria. It was helmed by Punit Malhotra. Alia appeared in a song in the second part.

title: Delhi HC directs police to decide within one week Karni Sena’s plea to hold protest at Jantar Mantar
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

New Delhi, The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the city police to decide within a week a plea by Kshatriya Karni Sena president Raj Shekhawat seeking permission to hold a protest against the of late notified UGC equity regulations at Jantar Mantar here.

Adding to this, Delhi HC directs police to decide within one week Karni Sena’s plea to hold protest at Jantar Mantar The high court was informed that while the protest was earlier scheduled for September 6, the petitioner has now changed the date to September 20 in view of the soon-to-release BRICS Summit in the national capital.

Meanwhile, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma directed petitioner Shekhawat to file a fresh application with the Delhi Police seeking permission to hold the peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar on September 20 from 10 am to 5 pm.
Notably, Initially, the petitioner had challenged denial of permission by Delhi Police to hold the protest at September 6.

As per the latest buzz, However, after being suggested by the court to change the date as the police were not allowing the protest on that day in view of the BRICS Summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, the petitioner shifted it to September 20.
In further updates, The high court on Monday directed that the fresh application be placed before the competent authority which will decide it within a week by September 14.
On top of that, When the counsel for the police urged the court to grant time till September 16-17, the bench made it clear that the application has to be decided by September 14.
"Certainly not. September 14 means 14. You have to decide the application by September 14. You may impose any condition or direction on them which is appropriate as per law," Justice Sharma shared.

title: Mirzapur The Movie worldwide box office collection: Gangster saga mints ₹132 crore, overtakes Hanuman Ansh, beats Alpha
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Mirzapur The Movie worldwide ticket-window earnings day 3: It took all of three days for Mirzapur : The Movie to coast past the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark worldwide. Buoyed by excellent domestic collections, the gangster action thriller has now become the number one movie at the Indian ticket-window and is on its way to becoming a certified smash hit.

Adding to this, Mirzapur The Movie worldwide ticket-window earnings day 3: Divyenndu, Pankaj Tripathi, and Ali Fazal reunite for the movie. Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window update The Mirzapur movie had a spectacular opening at the domestic ticket-window on Friday. Lifted by exceptional response in mass centres of UP and Bihar, the movie minted ₹ 25 crore rupees on its first day. On Saturday, it saw a jump of over 25%, minting ₹ 32 crore rupees, and on Sunday, it saw another jump, earning ₹ 36 crore rupees. This gave the movie a three-day haul of ₹ 93.75 crore rupees net ( ₹ 112.35 crore rupees gross). This is one of the best opening weekends for an Indian movie this year, and certainly the best ever by a Hindi movie without any big star. On Sunday, Mirzapur: The Movie saw occupancy of almost 67% for its Hindi version, with the night shows almost 75% full across India.

Meanwhile, The bulk of Mirzapur’s earnings has come from India, but it has been a success overseas as well. The movie started off slowly internationally, but then picked up over the weekend. By Sunday, it had collected an impressive $2.1 million overseas, largely from North America and the Middle East. This takes the movie’s worldwide haul after three days to ₹ 132 crore rupees.

Notably, Mirzapur: The Movie entered the top-10 highest-grossing Hindi films of the year with its haul on Sunday. With a worldwide gross of ₹ 132 crore rupees, it now sits in the 8th spot. Its entry in the list meant that Alpha, the Alia Bhatt-starrer that collected ₹ 98 crore rupees worldwide, was edged out of the top 10. On Sunday, Mirzapur: The Movie also overtook the lifetime collections of two other successes - Main Vaapas Aaunga ( ₹ 99 crore rupees) and Raja Shivaji ( ₹ 130 crore rupees). Its stupendous Sunday also enabled the gangster drama to overtake another Hindi movie that is making waves in cinemas right now - Hanuman Ansh. The devotional movie has a gross of ₹ 125 crore rupees as of Sunday, with Mirzapur outpacing it in day-to-day collections.

As per the latest buzz, Presented by Amazon MGM Studios and Excel Entertainment, Mirzapur: The Movie is directed by Gurmeet Singh, written by Puneet Krishna, and produced by Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar under the banner of Excel Entertainment. The movie is co-produced by Kassim Jagmagia and Vishal Ramchandani. Mirzapur is set for a theatrical rollout in Hindi and Telugu on 4 September.

In further updates, The movie stars Ali Fazal, Pankaj Tripathi and Divyenndu, while Jitendra Kumar takes over from Vikrant Massey, who played Bablu Pandit in the show. Ravi Kishan, Abhishek Banerjee, Rasika Dugal, Mohitt Maalik, Sheeba Chadha, Rajesh Tailang, Pramod Pathak, Shriya Pilgaonkar, Harshita Shekhar Gaur, Shweta Tripathi, and Sonal S Chauhan round off the cast.

On top of that, Abhimanyu Mathur is Deputy Editor, Entertainment at Hindustan Times. With almost 15 years of experience in writing about everything from films and TV shows to cricket matches and elections, he inhales and exhales pop culture and news. Currently, he watches movies and TV shows and talks to celebrities for a living, while occasionally writing about them as well. A journalism graduate of Delhi College of Arts and Commerce, Delhi University, Abhimanyu began his career with Hindustan Times at the age of 20, swapping classrooms for newsrooms at an early age. He began his journey in the early days of digital journalism, later switching to the madness of print journalism. Work has led him to far off places like Japan and Jordan, as well as to the interiors of Haryana and the Indo-Pak border. He dabbled in city reporting in places like Meerut, Gurgaon, and Delhi, covered the Olympics and Cricket World Cups, before finding his calling in entertainment and lifestyle during the pandemic. A Rotten Tomatoes Certified Movie Critic, he is equally at home covering stories on ground as he is interviewing celebrities and studios, and sometimes prefers to shepherd teams in delivering traffic through the day. Even as his role has evolved from reporter to supervisor over the years, his first love remains writing (and of late, talking on camera). With a good understanding of cinema and its trends, and a keen eye for detail, he continues to spark conversations around showbiz for readers around the world. Read More

title: Diljit Dosanjh politely corrects fan for pairing Ik Onkar with his name on T-shirt, wins praise: ‘He is so humble’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Diljit Dosanjh has won millions of hearts around the globe with his music, and the singer continues to do so with his concerts worldwide. At his latest concert in Milan, the singer was seen greeting a foreign couple on stage. However, he gently corrected the fan over a T-shirt that featured the Sikh symbol Ik Onkar alongside his name.

Adding to this, Diljit Dosanjh sweetly corrected a fan at his recent Milan concert. Diljit politely corrects fan In a video from the concert, Diljit is seen welcoming the couple from the audience onto the stage. However, he noticed the fan's custom-printed white T-shirt, which featured both the sacred Sikh symbol Ik Onkar and Diljit's name side by side.

Meanwhile, Quickly noticing the symbol, Diljit gently placed his hand over the shirt and appeared to disapprove of the pairing. Diljit politely explained in English to the couple, "This is God... This is very special... and my name together, no, no." He insisted that the sacred symbol is divine and should not be placed alongside his own name.

Notably, However, Diljit was also quick to recognise the fan's intention and defend him in Punjabi: "I respect your feelings. Inhe pata nahi, maaf kar do please (He didn't know, please forgive him). But I respect you... Ek Onkar, mere walon saare ek ne (To me, everyone is one)." He then gave the couple a gift.
As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mera Diljit (@meradiljit)

In further updates, Many users commented on the video and lauded Diljit's gesture. A fan wrote, "He is so humble. That is why he is at the highest heights.. Bless him." Another comment read, "You are a very good Soul Diljit ♥️ Love n happiness always be showered on you by Babaji." One more comment read, "You rock brother ❤️🔥 love you respect from heart."

On top of that, Diljit is currently on his Europe tour. He was in Milan of late, and before that, he spent some time in Prague, where he explored the city by boat. title: Taapsee Pannu on not getting commercial films after Shah Rukh Khan's Dunki: 'Talent isn’t enough’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Taapsee Pannu is known for niche, hard-hitting cinema, but the star had a brush with mainstream Bollywood when she starred opposite Shah Rukh Khan in his 2023 movie Dunki . Compared to Shah Rukh's previous outings, Pathaan and Jawan, Dunki's performance at the ticket-window was seen as relatively subpar. However, for Taapsee it was the biggest commercial success of her career.

Adding to this, Taapsee Pannu spoke about mainstream cinema. In a recent interaction, the star spoke about how the movie did not lead to her being cast in more mainstream films and why she believes talent alone is often not enough to land such projects.

Meanwhile, In conversation with News18, Taapsee argued that female leads in mainstream films are often inconsequential and replaceable. She shared that actresses who have stronger industry connections and greater visibility tend to have an advantage when it comes to bagging such roles, something she feels she lacks.

Notably, She shared, “I feel that all actors are replaceable. It’s not like ki yeh role iske ilaava koi aur kar hi nahi sakta. They may do it differently but I think everyone can pull off every role. But the female characters in these so-called mainstream and commercial films are ones that can be played by anyone. And the basis of landing these roles isn’t your talent It’s your market, saleability, contacts, visbility, presence and influence. All of these factors more than an star’s talent come into play. And I know it for a fact that I’m lagging behind when it comes to these factors. The only basis on which I can get a movie is my talent. The only reason I got to work on Dunki is because Raju sir had seen my work. He puts his foot down for me."

As per the latest buzz, Taapsee gave full credit to Rajkumar Hirani for casting her in Dunki and for making what she described as an unconventional casting choice. She also admitted that such instances are not very common in the industry, which is why she feels she has not gone on to land more big-ticket mainstream films.

In further updates, She added, “Usually, the characters in a commercial movie aren’t significant enough and so, it doesn’t matter which star is playing the part. If an star fits into their budget and has a certain market value, they immediately cast her. Mainstream films that cast an star purely on the basis of talent are far and few. And directors like Raju sir, who are so sure of the star they want, are even fewer."

On top of that, Taapsee was last seen in Gandhari, which follows a mother's relentless pursuit to find and rescue her kidnapped daughter. The movie explores themes of revenge and redemption as she embarks on a harrowing journey to bring her daughter home. Gandhari received mixed to negative reviews from critics and audiences.

title: '6 saal jail me nahi seekhi': Sanjay Dutt refuses Maharashtra minister's 'speak Marathi' request on stage. Watch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Sanjay Dutt used his signature irreverent charm to avoid being caught off guard at a recent event in Mumbai. The star was on stage with Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik on Sunday when the minister asked him to speak in Marathi. But the Bollywood star made a joke at his own expense and quickly deflected the topic.

Adding to this, Sanjay Dutt with Mahrashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik. Sanjay Dutt sidesteps minister’s Marathi request In videos from the event circulating on social media, Sanjay and Sarnaik can be seen standing on the stage, with other dignitaries behind them. At one point, the minister says, “Aajkal main sab logon ko Marathi sikha raha hoon (These days, I am teaching everyone Marathi).” This was in reference to Sarnaik’s department’s recent ruling that autorickshaw drivers in Mumbai need a functional understanding of Marathi phrases to continue to work in the city. This controversial ruling has ruffled feathers across the city. After a few laughs at that statement, the minister continued in Marathi, “ So I thought after his entry, let us all get Sanjay Dutt to talk in Marathi. He speaks in Hindi, but all of us understand Marathi.”

Meanwhile, Sanjay Dutt then takes the mic and responds, “Pratap bhai. Main 6 saal jail me raha, Yervada mein. Tab bhi Marathi nahi seekh paaya. Main thoda seekha tha. (I was in the Yervada Jail for six years, and even there I didn’t learn Marathi. I learnt a little).” The star then put his arm around Sarnaik, calling him his old friend and brother, and added, “ Main Pratap bhai ka aabhaari hoon ki mujhe yahan bulaye. Hamara rishta bahut purana hai, 25 saal ho gaye hain (I am grateful to Pratap bhai for calling me here. We go way back, almost 25 years).”

Notably, There were polarising reactions to Sanjay Dutt’s candid admission on stage, with some praising the star for how he handled the situation. “Only Sanjay Dutt or Salman Khan can defy a minister like this and still smile,” chuckled one. Another added, “He ignored it with style.” Many others pointed out the irony that autorickshaw drivers in the city don’t have this option. “If only autowallahs could say this and avoid heavy fines too.”

As per the latest buzz, Many, however, were disappointed that Sanjay couldn’t speak Marathi despite living in Maharashtra all his life. “Sanjay Dutt has been living in Mumbai for more than 50 years, and he himself says that even after spending 6 years in Yerwada Jail, he still couldn’t learn Marathi. And he openly admitted this in front of everyone, without any shame,” read one tweet.

title: Grand Tamasha: Decoding economic drivers of Gen Z protests, jobs debate
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

This summer, thousands of young Indians took to the streets to demand sweeping reforms of the higher education sector. This unexpected wave of Gen Z mobilisation was catalysed by the emergence of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical meme page that blossomed into a national movement. Protests that began over the state of higher education soon tapped into something much larger: growing frustration among young Indians over jobs, economic opportunity, and their prospects for the future.

Adding to this, Mahambare elaborated on her views on Grand Tamasha about the economic roots of Gen Z protests, education-linked unemployment, agricultural exits, and India's urban housing crunch. (Representational) India’s jobs debate is often framed around a familiar set of concerns: too many people working in agriculture, too few manufacturing jobs, an economy that is too-services oriented, and stubbornly high unemployment among the young. But not all of these truisms about the Indian economy are actually borne out by the data, argues economist Vidya Mahambare.

Meanwhile, Mahamabare elaborated on her views on the season premiere of Grand Tamasha, a weekly podcast on Indian politics and policy co-produced by HT and the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Mahambare is the Union Bank Chair Professor of Economics and Director at the Great Lakes Institute of Management in Chennai. She studies central banking and monetary policy, structural transformation, labour market dynamics and gender economics.

Notably, Mahambare spoke with Grand Tamasha host Milan Vaishnav about the economic drivers of the Gen Z protests, the link between unemployment and education, and the futility of the manufacturing versus services debate. She also discussed the exodus of young people from the agricultural sector, the misleading headlines on female labour force participation, and India’s acute urban housing shortage.

As per the latest buzz, Mahambare highlighted the fact that, in India, it is the India’s richest states that have the highest rates of youth unemployment. “In prosperous states like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Telangana, unemployment among young people is high, which seems counter-intuitive. In these states, education levels are higher, and more men and women are looking for jobs, so the labour force is simply larger. Second, educated people want a specific kind of job, so they wait for it. To wait, you need a kind of privilege,” she explained. “In poorer states, unemployment is low, but it’s because fewer people, especially women, are looking for work. Men there can’t wait long; whatever job comes up, they have to take it quickly because there’s no family support.”

In further updates, The economist also took issue with the oft-repeated claim that India needs to get more young people out of agriculture. “If we look at people in the age group of 20 to 29, currently only 13% of young adults in India are working in agriculture. Twenty years back, that number was 34%,” she shared.

On top of that, “Structural transformation among today’s young has already taken place. The median age of agricultural labor is now 53 in Kerala, 48 in Tamil Nadu, and 40 in all of India. If we push for more people to leave, it will be young people who go.”

Mahambare shared the time is ripe to think about how “we discuss agriculture as an industry, an occupation, and how we help raise incomes within it rather than talking as if the transformation hasn’t happened, because among the young it’s nearly complete.”

title: Varun Dhawan says Hanuman Ansh is not a film but a ‘divine experience’; lauds Shobhinaw Satyaa's ‘brilliant acting’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

A tiny ₹ 2-crore rupees Bollywood movie with no major stars, Hanuman Ansh , has become the talk of the town. The movie has been creating waves at the ticket-window and has so far collected over ₹ 100 crore rupees. Amid its success, Bollywood star Varun Dhawan posted on Instagram to share a video praising the movie and urging audiences to watch it in theatres.

Adding to this, Varun Dhawan is mesmerised by Hanuman Ansh. Varun Dhawan is all praise for Hanuman Ansh On Sunday, Varun posted on Instagram story to reveal that he had watched Hanuman Ansh with his mother in a theatre. He shared, "Please go to the theatre and watch Hanuman Ansh. I just went with my mom, and it was an amazing experience. Take your parents, go with your friends. I highly recommend this movie to everyone. No one had told me to make this video, neither had anyone called me; I just wanted to do this. I have had a connection with Lord Hanuman since childhood, but this is something else. This is a purely made movie. I will not even call it a movie; it’s something divine. You go and experience it."

Meanwhile, He further lauded the movie’s direction and performances, saying, "Shobhinaw Satyaa ji is brilliant in the movie. What a performance. And Visha ji, the direction you did, hats off. Brilliant stuff. Please everyone go and watch the movie."

Notably, Varun is not the first Bollywood star to praise Hanuman Ansh. Before him, Kangana Ranaut also lauded the movie and called it a "satsang". She urged audiences to skip their therapy sessions and instead watch the movie in theatres. Filmmakers Madhur Bhandarkar and Aditya Dhar have also voiced their support for the movie.

As per the latest buzz, Directed and produced by Vishal Chaturvedi under his banner Swambhu Media Network, the movie is based on his book Divine Detour: That Changed My Life, which chronicles the life of Neem Karoli Baba. It stars Shobhinaw Satyaa and Chandan Anand in the lead roles.

In further updates, The movie follows the early life of a young boy, Lakshmi Narayan, in pre-Independence India. After the death of his mother, he leaves home in search of God and embarks on a journey across North India, eventually transforming into Neem Karoli Baba.

On top of that, The movie opened to low box-office numbers, collecting just ₹ 10 lakh on its first day. However, positive word-of-mouth changed the course of its box-office run. In its third week, the movie picked up pace and recorded its highest single-day collection on day 24, when it collected ₹ 12.75 crore rupees.

In its fourth weekend, the movie collected a total of ₹ 39.25 crore rupees, taking its total India net collection to ₹ 122.13 crore rupees. Despite competition from films such as Mirzapur: The Movie and Toxic, Hanuman Ansh has continued to enjoy a dream run at the ticket-window.

Adding to this, Karan Johar is the son of late movie producer Yash Johar. Karan Johar remembers dad Yash Johar Sharing a childhood photograph of himself with Yash Johar, the filmmaker wrote, “Happy birthday papa, miss you every day.”

title: Mirzapur: The Movie faces controversy as Rapperiya Baalam alleges his song was used without permission
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Rapperiya Baalam has alleged that his song ‘Shoorveer’ was used in Mirzapur: The Movie without permission or credit and questioned its use in a gangster scene.

Adding to this, The movie rolled out in theatres on Friday, September 4. Rapperiya Baalam subsequently posted on Instagram to express his disappointment over the song’s inclusion in a sequence featuring gangsters.

Meanwhile, “Today, my heart is broken. Some of you may ask why my heart is broken. You might say I should be happy because my song is in Mirzapur. But the Mirzapur team did not take my permission to use my song. Who gave them the permission? I certainly did not,” he shared.

Notably, According to the artist, ‘ Shoorveer’ was specifically created as a tribute to Maharana Pratap. He questioned the decision to use the song in a sequence that, in his view, presents the movie’s gangsters in a glorified manner.
As per the latest buzz, “This song is dedicated to Maharana Pratap ji. We are using this song to glorify the villains in the movie. Is this right?” he shared.
In further updates, Rapperiya Baalam also shared he would have been open to collaborating with the team had they approached him directly.

On top of that, “If the Mirzapur team had approached me and shared, 'Rapperiya bhai, we want to use your song,' we would have given them 10 ideas. But taking the song without permission is not right,” he shared.
The artist further raised questions about the copyright and licensing process involved in using the track.

title: Twin sisters jailed in Iran over anti-regime protests: Ripped-out hair, broken elbows, and a ‘rape threat’
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Two teenage twin sisters were taken from their beds in the middle of the night by masked men, later identified as those of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. For what? For as per reports joining millions of protesters in the agitation against the regime led by Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in January 2026.

Adding to this, Taraneh (L) and Romina (R) Rahimi took part in the protests against the Iranian regime on January 8 and 9 this year. (X/@AlinejadMasih /@BabakTaghvaee1) However, Marzieh Nourmohammadi, the mother of the twins, Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, had no clue where her daughters were for four months. She searched hospitals, state facilities, everywhere she could possibly search for them, only to learn that they had been seized by the IRGC. She had received a call, saying, "We have your girls; come to see them at the prison."
Meanwhile, The mother finally got to visit them in prison in May, but she couldn't recognise her own daughters.
Notably, A US-based cousin of the twins shared they had bruises on their faces, broken elbows, and had extremely patchy scalps from being dragged around by their hair, The Guardian reported.
As per the latest buzz, Taraneh was as per reports told that the prison guards would rape her twin, Romina, in front of her unless they signed a confession.

In further updates, Around four months have passed since the mother visited her twins at the Dowlatabad prison in Iran's Isfahan city. It has now as per reports been learned that an Iranian court has sentenced Taraneh to death for her participation in the January protests against the regime, while Romina has been given a 25-year prison term.
On top of that, Since the sentencing, neither of the women has been seen by their family.

"There is an 18-day period that lawyers can go and appeal, but in a lot of (execution) cases of late, that has not happened. They just sentence and take the kids and execute them and hang them. So, I mean, nothing really makes sense," he was quoted as saying.
