title: Exclusive | Hanuman Ansh's 21-yr-old producer Anupriya Nagar on sequel: Maharaj ji gave us a lot, we don't have a choice
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

At 21, Anupriya Nagar invested all the money she had collected and saved from three years of part-time jobs in the UK into her first movie, Hanuman Ansh, despite having no filmmaking experience. A graduate of economics from the University of Bath, she had even got a job in Zurich before returning to India in 2025 and eventually getting involved with the movie as a co-producer. “I feel like age is just a number,” she says. “My only focus was to bring Maharaj ji’s ( Neem Karoli Baba ) stories to the younger audience, to Gen Z. We get to know about such things through foreigners. I myself got to know about him through a foreigner and, being the youth of India, I was ashamed that I was not getting to know about him through his own story.”

Adding to this, Anupriya Nagar View this post on Instagram For her, backing Hanuman Ansh was never about financial returns. “This was the risk I was willing to take. I collected this money in the three years that I studied in the UK, doing part-time jobs. When I came across Maharaj ji at a beautiful juncture of my life, I just wanted to get into this project. I didn’t know what I could contribute because I had not done filmmaking, but I was ready to give my heart and soul to it. The project needed some investment at that particular time, so I shared, ‘Whatever I have, I’m ready to give you guys.’”

Meanwhile, Her family initially worried about the decision. “My father was protective. He shared, ‘You don’t know much about filmmaking and you know how the industry is. You’re so young.’ But when I told him I was making a movie on a noble saint and narrated the story, he was fine. They’ve been with me through thick and thin. In fact, I think they do more publicity for the movie than I do!”

Notably, The movie’s ticket-window journey has since surprised everyone. After opening on 300 screens and dropping to just 30 on its eighth day, it eventually expanded to over 1,500 screens, and now releasing internationally. It has also touched the ₹ 100 crore rupees figure. “My ticket-window is people knowing about Maharaj ji,” she says. “But the collections reassure me that people are interested in this kind of content. People are making an effort to get his darshan in theatres.”

As per the latest buzz, The movie ends with a promise of a sequel, and Anupriya confirms it will happen, “We are not going to dishearten our viewers. Maharaj ji has given us so much in abundance regarding the ticket-window, so we don’t have a choice but to make this.”

In further updates, More importantly, she wants the sequel to retain the simplicity of the first movie. “Our movie was supposed to be made in ₹ 2 crore rupees. If we had made the same movie in ₹ 10 crore rupees, it wouldn’t have come out this way. The rawness and simplicity came from the low budget, and we will definitely keep that in mind,” Anupriya ends.

On top of that, Rishabh Suri writes for the daily Entertainment & Lifestyle supplement HT City. From Bollywood to Hollywood, from Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam films, to OTT and television- he covers it all.

title: ‘Too bad if someone doesn't see it as feminine’: Masaba Gupta hails Bipasha Basu, takes a dig at Mrunal Thakur's remark
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Bipasha Basu stunned one and all with her new pictures for a cover shoot for Elle India. The star has now received a shoutout from fashion designer Masaba Gupta, who lauded her beauty and muscular build. In her praise, Masaba refered to a previous comment made by star Mrunal Thakur that had caused an internet storm last year. In the clip, Mrunal had called Bipasha Basu "manly with muscles", claiming she is "better" than her.

Adding to this, Masaba then added, “And @bipashabasu I love your athletic build. I love the muscle- and I want more thanks to the standard of fitness you set. Too bad if someone doesn't see it as feminine. This is so great. Welcome back. Breath of fresh air.”

Meanwhile, In the interview done sometime in 2012, Mrunal joked that she is much better than ‘muscular’ Bipasha Basu. Ever since the video surfaced on Reddit last year and then migrated to Instagram, Bipasha's followers made edits to recall just how beautiful and iconic she used to be. Many were even disappointed with Mrunal's comments, saying they are no longer her followers.

Notably, Mrunal later wrote a post on Instagram stories, expressing regret at what was shared. "19-year-old me as a teenager shared many silly things. I didn’t always understand the weight of my voice or how much words, even in jest, could hurt. But it did, and for that I am deeply sorry. My intent was never to body-shame anyone. It was playful banter in an interview, that went too far. But I understand how it came across, and I truly wish I had chosen my words differently. With time, I’ve grown to appreciate that beauty comes in every form, and that’s something I truly value now,” she shared.

title: ‘Pathaan hoon, goli maar do’: Sanjay Gupta says Shah Rukh Khan was 'only guy' who refused to bow to underworld threats
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Shah Rukh Khan rose to stardom in the 90s when Bollywood was still under the shadow and threats of the underworld. From movie stars to directors, everyone was a target, recalled filmmaker Sanjay Gupta in a new interaction with Hussain Zaidi Files on their YouTube channel. However, if there was one person who refused any offer from them, it was Shah Rukh Khan.

Adding to this, Shah Rukh Khan as per reports refused to bow down to pressure from the underworld. (File/AFP) What Sanjay Gupta shared During the chat, Sanjay shared, “I have seen the underworld in its peak in Bombay… There was one Punjabi star, he was found dead at Movie City, and it was later disclosed that he was an informant. Manisha Koirala's secretary, such a simple fellow, and then one fine day someone walked to his office and shot him dead. Then they fired at Rakesh Roshan ji… we were open, soft targets. These are not extortion calls but these are different…”

Meanwhile, He went on to add that almost every top star and star were signed in the papers for films that would be made. He added that they would come on set and see the shooting as well. "The only guy in the movie industry, Shah Rukh Khan, when he was threatened, he shared, ‘Picture to kabhi nahi karunga, show kabhi nahi karunga. Pathaan hoon, goli maarni hai maar do (I will never do the movie or show, I am a Pathaan, just shoot me if you want)’. I am not scared of you, but I will not work with you and not do shows for you. He actually collected their respect. They also must have felt that there’s at least one person…” shared Sanjay.

Notably, Earlier, while speaking on a podcast with Ranveer Allahbadia, even filmmaker Farah Khan had admitted that pressure did exist in the 90s. When she was asked whether the three Khans were pressurised by the underworld, Farah shared, “Yes.” When further questioned about Shah Rukh receiving a call, she shared, “I don't know. But, I know that during Duplicate or Kuch Kuch Hota Hai premiere, Karan had got a underworld threat, and it was very scary. Everyone was discussing whether the premiere should be cancelled or we should go ahead with it.”

As per the latest buzz, Shah Rukh dabbled in theatre and had his first starring role in the 1988 TV show Dil Dariya. However, due to production delays, Fauji marked his acting debut, and the series based on army cadets made him a household name. He also starred in TV shows like Circus, Idiot, Umeed and Wagle Ki Duniya after that.

In further updates, Despite gaining fame, Shah Rukh wasn’t initially interested in acting. It was only after his mother’s death in 1990 that he changed his mind and moved to Mumbai from Delhi to pursue a career in Bollywood. He debuted on the silver screen with the 1992 movie Deewana, and there has been no looking back after that.
On top of that, Following the rollout of the 2023 films Pathaan and Jawan, Shah Rukh will star in Siddharth Anand’s King, slated for rollout in December 2026.

title: Mirzapur The Movie box office collection day 3 (updated live): Gangster saga is an unstoppable force, crosses ₹70 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window earnings day 3: The Mirzapur juggernaut is not stopping anytime soon. Many had wondered whether people would want to pay to watch a movie based on a web series in theatres. But over the last three days, Mirzapur The Movie has answered that, with cold, hard numbers. The movie opened spectacularly and, since then, has gone from strength to strength, ending its opening weekend just shy of the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark, a phenomenal achievement for a movie without a major star.

Adding to this, Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window earnings day 3: Ali Fazal returns as Guddu Pandit in Mirzapur. Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window update The Mirzapur movie was expected to open well ever since its first teaser was rolled out earlier this year. But even its most ardent supporters were surprised by how well it has done, particularly in UP, Bihar, and Delhi, the centres traditionally open to mass action. The movie opened at ₹ 25 crore rupees net on Friday, one of the biggest openings for a Bollywood movie this year. On Saturday, it saw a jump of over 25%, minting ₹ 32 crore rupees. This gave the movie a two-day haul of ₹ 57.75 crore rupees net. According to Sacnilk, Mirzapur The Movie has collected ₹ 14 crore rupees net by 3 PM on its third day. This takes its opening weekend haul to ₹ 71 crore rupees . The movie is outpacing both its Friday and Saturday hauls as of now. The morning shows recorded footfalls of around 38%, a stellar figure for a movie of this scale. The movie should get close to ₹ 100 crore rupees net by the end of the day, and aim to cross that mark by Monday itself.

Meanwhile, Normally, a ₹ 90 crore rupees opening weekend in Hindi is the domain of the A-listers or select pan-India stars. Very few actors, apart from the three Khans, Akshay Kumar, and Hrithik Roshan, have managed this consistently. Mirzapur has put the likes of Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, and Divyenndu in this league. The bumper opening weekend also means that Mirzapur The Movie has already surpassed the lifetime collections of a few recent releases, including the Alia Bhatt- and Sharvari-starrer Alpha ( ₹ 60 crore rupees).

title: Mirzapur song Shoorveer irks original singer, called insult to Rajasthanis: ‘Meant for Rana Pratap, used for villains?’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Mirzapur : The Movie was rolled out in theatres on Friday and has performed well at the ticket-window after receiving rave reviews. However, the makers have now been accused of using a song in the movie meant for Maharana Pratap for a scene featuring gangsters. Rajasthani artist Rapperiya Baalam took to his Instagram to allege that it was also used without his permission or credit.

Adding to this, Rapperiya Baalam's Shoorveer was as per reports featured in Mirzapur: The Movie in a gangster scene. Rapperiya Baalam says Mirzapur makers have insulted Rajasthanis Rapperiya posted a video on Instagram, saying he never imagined posting like this someday. “Aaj to dil dukhaya hai (You have hurt me),” he says. He shared many will ask him why he’s hurt when his song has been featured in a movie like Mirzapur. “The team never took my permission to use the song. This song was dedicated to Maharana Pratap Singh, and you’re using it to glorify villains? Is this okay?” he questioned.

Meanwhile, Rapperiya also shared that if the Mirzapur team had approached him after they liked the song, he would’ve given them ten such alternatives. “But to use it without permission…I don’t know who you took the rights from. I am hurt because I feel like you’ve insulted Rajasthan and Maharana Pratap ji. It’s not something I can digest,” shared the musician, pointing out that the warrior had faced a lot for the country.
Notably, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rapperiya Baalam (@rapperiya_baalam)

As per the latest buzz, The internet was angry at the Mirzapur makers for using a song meant for Maharana Pratap for gangsters. An Instagram page named Folk Music of Rajasthan spoke up in the musician’s support, writing, “History is meant to be respected, not mixed with crime dramas for cheap entertainment value. As a Rajasthani i want to say please Do not mock the sacrifices of our heroes. Stop misrepresenting Rajasthani culture. #respecthistory #maharanapratap #shoorveer #saverajasthaniculture.”
In further updates, View this post on Instagram A post shared by FOLK 🇮🇳 (@folkmusicofrajasthan)

On top of that, They also wrote, “The song “Shoorveer” was written to celebrate the legacy and dignity of warriors. Turning around and inserting it into a gangster drama without the artist’s knowledge is bad enough but denying Rapperiya Baalam his rightful credits while everyone else gets theirs? That’s where the industry fails its independent creators. Mainstream platforms need to stop diluting regional history and bypassing legal courtesy.”

Numerous others also pointed out that the makers of Mirzapur should’ve approached Rapperiya before using the song. “This is how the mainstream has repeatedly diluted and distorted Rajasthan’s history,” read one comment. “This is completely wrong. You cannot use someone’s song without their permission. Please file a copyright claim. We are with you and fully support you,” wrote another.

title: Singer Akriti Kakar: Even established singers struggle for opportunities; films and indie songs both are tough to crack
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Singer Akriti Kakar , known for tracks such as Saturday Saturday ( Humpty Sharma Ki Dulhania , 2014) and Iski Uski ( 2 States , 2014) says that even established artistes continue to face challenges in the music industry. From landing playback opportunities to making independent music click, singers continue to face uncertainty.

Adding to this, Akriti Kakkar The 40-year-old, who of late rolled out her song Oh Jaanu with Euphoria member Palash Sen , points out that playback singing comes with too many variables. “Sometimes I just have to wait for a music director to call me for a song in a movie. Even when I get the opportunity, there’s no guarantee that the song will make it to the final movie. And even if it does, you never know whether the movie or the song will work,” she says.
Meanwhile, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Akriti Kakar (@akritikakar)
Notably, With independent music offering an alternative, Kakar believes artistes should take charge of creating their own opportunities rather than waiting for that one breakthrough song.

As per the latest buzz, “The only thing in the hand of a singer is to do their best, that’s it! So why not use that energy for your own song, alongside being called by other people? Otherwise, I will just keep waiting for that one life-changing song,” says the singer.

In further updates, “There are so many songs being rolled out every day and there’s every chance of your song getting lost in the crowd. It can be discouraging, and at times, the thought of giving up and not doing it again comes to the mind. But as singers, our karma is to keep trying,” she says.
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Akriti Kakar (@akritikakar)

The singer says, “ Everytime I do a show I put some money aside for my indie song. We have to become business people also. So, most of my music is made and funded by me and my husband Chirag Arora (an ad movie maker) has done the visual side of it. As an artist, I am trying to make music that I want to say with a blend of nostalgia and modernity. And, I try to do it differently from the existing flow.”

title: Hanuman Ansh crosses ₹100 crore at the box office, smallest Bollywood film to do so; beats Singham, 83 lifetime hauls
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Two weeks after its near-miraculous revival at the ticket-window, devotional movie Hanuman Ansh has crossed ₹ 100 crore rupees in net domestic ticket-window collections. The movie, based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba , is the smallest Hindi movie (in terms of scale) ever to enter the 100-crore rupees club. The movie is on course to register its biggest weekend yet, in its fifth week in theatres.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh is now a ₹100 crore rupees movie. Hanuman Ansh hits ₹ 100 crore rupees at the ticket-window Hanuman Ansh opened on a dismal note, earning only ₹ 10 lakh on its opening day, and closing its first two weeks with a net haul of just ₹ 1.48 crore rupees. On its 16th day in theatres, the movie saw a sizable jump in earnings. As word of mouth spread, Hanuman Ansh saw record-breaking third and fourth weeks at the ticket-window. It minted ₹ 61 crore rupees in its fourth week alone. The upward trend continued into its fifth weekend, with the movie netting ₹ 10 crore rupees on Friday and ₹ 16.50 crore rupees on Saturday. This took its domestic haul to just above ₹ 99 crore rupees. On Sunday morning, the morning shows took Hanuman Ansh past the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark. It is now the 143rd Hindi movie to cross the mark. With a budget of ₹ 2 crore rupees, Hanuman Ansh is the smallest Hindi movie to enter this famed club, beating The Kashmir Files ( ₹ 15 crore rupees) by a substantial margin.

Meanwhile, As of 1 PM on Sunday, the movie’s domestic collection stands at just over ₹ 105 crore rupees. This has helped the devotional movie beat the final collections of several films much bigger than itself. On Sunday, it soared past the lifetime haul of sports drama 83 ( ₹ 104 crore rupees), Salman Khan’s Sikandar ( ₹ 103 crore rupees), Ajay Devgn’s Singham ( ₹ 100 crore rupees), and the Hindi version of Allu Arjun’s Pushpa The Rise ( ₹ 105 crore rupees). The movie is primed to do better with its international rollout this month.

Notably, Written and directed by Vishal Chaturvedi, Hanuman Ansh follows a grieving young man, Lakshminarayan, who embarks on a spiritual journey in search of God after his mother's death. As he travels across North India in search of answers to life, death, and human suffering, he eventually becomes the revered saint Neem Karoli Baba.
As per the latest buzz, The movie stars Shobhinaw Satya in the lead role alongside Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi, Gulshan Pandey and Bhagvandas Patel.

title: All That Breathes director Shaunak Sen's next tells the story of his own cancer battle: ‘A way to displace the terror’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Indian filmmaker Shaunak Sen is turning his lens inwards for his new documentary after the Oscar-nominated All That Breathes. In a recent interview, the filmmaker shared that his next movie began as a "coping" mechanism after a shock cancer diagnosis, but continues the motifs of environmental degradation and caregiving from his previous work.

Adding to this, Indian filmmaker Shaunak Sen reading notes from a diary at his residence in New Delhi. (Photo by Arun SANKAR / AFP) (AFP) Shaunak Sen on dealing with ‘terror’ In an interview with AFP, the 39-year-old filmmaker opened up about his soon-to-release untitled documentary. “It became a kind of coping strategy, or a way to deal or dissociate or displace the terror of what you've just been told,” he shared, adding that his diagnosis brought home "the same risks" that make hundreds of birds fall every year from New Delhi's throat-burning polluted skies -- this time on “my own body”.

Meanwhile, Shaunak's All That Breathes follows two brothers running a largely self-funded clinic for birds falling victim to Delhi's polluted air. It won top documentary prizes at Sundance and Cannes in 2022 and was nominated for Best Documentary Feature at the 2023 Oscars .

Notably, “Whenever you ask most oncologists why this happened, or why this current giant spike in cancer rates is occurring, a lot of them would talk about environmental factors like toxins or chemicals or the air,” he added.

As per the latest buzz, Shaunak says the protagonist in his new movie is not him, but his doctor. “I did not want to make something that was solipsistically inwards folding. What I loved in a surgeon was the ability to completely lose yourself, to be immersed in the absolute present. That feels meditative and contemplative. It's a kind of melting away of everything extraneous, and you're in the pinprick of the moment,” he added.

In further updates, The movie is also about Sen's relationship with New Delhi, where he grew up, went to school and university, and where all his work is set. The filmmaker called the city a ‘wallpaper’ for the movie.

On top of that, In January 2025, the filmmaker opened up about his cancer diagnosis on social media. Shaunak posted on Instagram to talk about the health scare. He also shared several pictures of the hospital. One showed him in a hospital bed, and others featured his friends who visited him in the hospital, including director Mira Nair and Tillotama Shome.

“Bit of an absurd update. October end, during a checkup for an autoimmune thing, I got a shock diagnosis: a routine scan revealed a small malignant tumour in the kidney. Utter bolt from the blue. No kidney-related symptoms, no hereditary history, no big history of drinking/smoking. Urgent surgery was advised,” Shaunak wrote in the note.

title: 'Films with women in centre don't get producers' backing', laments Rasika Dugal: 'Difficult for them to get released'
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Rasika Dugal has shared that films with ‘women in the centre’ seldom find backers in Hindi cinema and often struggle for rollout. The star, who is currently starring in the Mirzapur movie, also opened up about the use of AI in screenwriting, a global ongoing debate.

Adding to this, Rasika Dugal plays Beena Tripathi in Mirzapur: The Movie. Rasika Dugal on women-led films in Bollywood In conversation with ANI, Rasika Dugal shared that she routinely receives scripts with strong female characters, but they later struggle to get the required backing. Talking about the state of Indian films, she added, “Writing might change with the help of AI. However, it is the distribution which becomes a problem. I get a lot of scripts every day which have very interesting characters, women in the centre, but they often don't have producers backing them. Or if they have, if those films have been made, it's difficult for them to get releases.”

Meanwhile, The star then elaborated on her view of the use of artificial intelligence, which is increasingly discussed as a tool that could assist filmmakers at different stages of the creative process, including idea development and writing. “I am not so much in favour of the idea of using AI; I feel that for writing, I feel that AI can be a supporting tool, but not the main thing,” the star shared, adding that she does not use AI extensively herself and therefore does not consider herself particularly well-versed with the technology.

Notably, Currently, the star is basking in the success of Mirzapur: The Movie, which sees her reprise her role as Beena Tripathi from the series. title: Hanuman Ansh to be made tax free in Uttarakhand, CM Pushkar Singh Dhami hails it for showing Neem Karoli Baba's penance
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

As it blazes past milestones at the ticket-window, there is more cheer for devotional movie Hanuman Ansh . Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami has opened up that the movie, based on the life and teachings of spiritual leader Neem Karoli Baba , will be made tax-free in the state.

Adding to this, Hanuman Ansh is based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba. Hanuman Ansh to be made tax-free On Friday, DM Dhami watched the movie at a cinema hall in Dehradun along with his wife Geeta Dhami, cabinet colleagues Ganesh Joshi and Pradeep Batra, and several MLAs. The CM shared films like Hanuman Ansh play a vital role in showcasing the state's spiritual and cultural heritage to the nation and the world.

Meanwhile, “Through the movie, we had the opportunity to know and understand Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj Ji's penance, sacrifice, service, and his unwavering faith in Lord Hanuman. His entire life was dedicated to the service of humanity, spiritual practice, and the welfare of society,” the chief minister shared in a post on X (formerly Twitter).

Notably, “The life of Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj Ji gives us the message that devotion is not merely practice, but also the path of service, surrender, and human welfare,” he added. Congratulating the movie's team for creating an “inspirational and spiritual movie”, he opened up that it would be made tax-free in the state.

In further updates, The movie stars Shobhinaw Satya in the lead role alongside Vihaan Shedge, Chandan K Anand, Purnima Tiwari, Anil Rastogi, Gulshan Pandey and Bhagvandas Patel.

By its second week, the movie was playing in fewer than 20 theatres across India. But then, it picked up by a strong word-of-mouth. It collected over ₹ 28 crore rupees net in India on its fourth weekend and since then, has raced towards the ₹ 100-crore rupees mark. title: Apoorva Mukhija says kalawa controversy was her breaking point: ‘I don't think God comes with rules’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Content creator and social media influencer Apoorva Mukhija , known as The Rebel Kid, faced severe online backlash earlier this year in April after posting a video where she cut off her sacred Hindu kalawa (mauli) thread with scissors ahead of attending the Coachella Music and Arts Festival. In a new video on her YouTube channel, Apoorva has broken silence on the row and shared that it was the breaking point for her after a series of controversies.

Adding to this, Apoorva Mukhija has broken her silence on the kalawa row. What Apoorva shared During the Storytime video, Apoorva shared, “After the Latent row, my mental health was so f****g bad that I constantly felt that I had no purpose in life. Whatever I do, I was getting abuses and cancelled. I was getting anxiety even after waking up. Tanmay Bhatt, Samay Raina had so much motivation to do something so much with her career. I had given up. I was not this person earlier, and my last breaking point was the kalawa row.”

Meanwhile, She detailed, “I was at Coachella and doing a get ready with me video. I cannot be normal and I had to make some jokes. So I was wearing the kalawa on my hand and I cut it saying that the thread would ruin my aesthetic. Now, my relationship with God is very new. I just started believing in God, it gives me a lot of peace. But I don't think God believes in rules, that he cares if I cut a thread or something. So when I was doing it I did not think it was wrong. I knew my God would not mind. But ofcourse other people who believed in the same God got upset about it… Even though I have seen bigger controversies in my life that was my breaking point truly. Whatever I do, I say, I cannot say anything right. I was mad, and no one knew how to handle me.”

Notably, Apoorva of late opened up that she has moved out of India to pursue her studies in New York, where she hopes to meet new people and experience a different life. She admitted that while moving to New York was a dream and she should be happy about it, she is also scared because her friends, career and everything she knows are in India. In New York, she will be living in a dorm and returning to student life. She opened up that she will be pursuing an MBA there.
As per the latest buzz, She had made her acting debut in Nadaaniyan. She was also seen in The Traitors Season 1 and most of late, in Lock Upp Season 2 , where she arrived as an informant.

title: Bipasha Basu calls out insensitive paparazzi for brutal body shaming after she gave birth: I went through major trolling
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Bipasha Basu has always been known in the Hindu movie industry as one of the fittest stars. She has also promoted fitness and health for women for many years. In a new cover for Elle India, Bipasha opened up about the standards for women's bodies and how they become topics for discussion on social media. The star, who welcomed her first child, a baby girl, on November 12, 2022, with Karan Singh Grover , shared that she faced intense trolling for her body.

Adding to this, Star Bipasha Basu opened up about facing trolling. (File Photo/ PTI) What Bipasha shared In the chat, Bipasha candidly spoke about the unrealistic expectations placed on women after giving birth. She shared, “The conversation around women’s bodies is quite bizarre even now. Magically, when you give birth, you are supposed to get back into the shape of your twenties even when you are in your forties. What's expected of a 20-year-old is expected of a 40-year-old. And if you’re not bouncing back, they’re going to troll you. They’re going to be massively brutal.”

Meanwhile, She went on to add, "I went through major, major trolling. A few insensitive paps took really bizarre pictures of me. They don’t see how much effort the woman must be putting in, how much they have to do with a baby, with their life, with their lifestyle and also their personal pressures. Nobody really cares. Everybody expects you to bounce back. I’m an extremely confident person, so no kind of trolling can break me. I know what my journey is, I know what work I need to put in, when I need to put it in, and I will go with that. Outside noise does not really matter.”
Notably, Bipasha is often seen sharing adorable family moments and fun memories with her daughter on social media.

As per the latest buzz, Karan and Bipasha first met on the sets of the movie Alone in 2015. Their on-screen chemistry soon blossomed into a real-life romance. The couple dated for nearly a year before tying the knot in April 2016. They have now been together for a decade and embraced parenthood when they welcomed their daughter, Devi Basu Singh Grover, on November 12, 2022, marking a beautiful new chapter in their lives.

In further updates, Bipasha was last seen in the web series Dangerous. Written by Vikram Bhatt and directed by Bhushan Patel, the series marked her OTT debut alongside Karan Singh Grover. The show also featured Sonali Raut, Natasha Suri, Suyyash Rai and Nitin Arora in key roles and is available to watch on MX Player. The star has been away from films for quite some time now.

title: Exclusive | Shoot for Sudhir Mishra's film, backed by Anubhav Sinha, with Manoj Bajpayee as Gandhi begins in Lucknow
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

National Award-winning filmmaker Sudhir Mishra ’s soon-to-release project, with the working title Gandhi and My Mother , has gone on floors. The movie’s shoot commenced with an outdoor sequence in Lucknow on Friday. Star Manoj Bajpayee plays Mahatma Gandhi in the movie.

Adding to this, Director Sudhir Mishra shooting for this next movie in Lucknow with star Manoj Bajpayee playing the role of Mahatma Gandhi The movie also features actors Divya Dutta and Saurabh Shukla .

Meanwhile, The Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi (2005) director had earlier told HT City, “My mother (Durga Devendra Nath Mishra) had met Gandhi as a child and we have had long discussions with her about him. Before she passed away (in 2022), I made a promise to her that I will make a movie on him. So, I wrote this script that deals with a chapter from the later stage of his life. Anubhav (Sinha, director-producer) has backed me.”

Notably, The shooting began at the Narhi locality near Lucknow Zoo, where a sequence featuring the young girl and Bapu’s public movement was picturised. The production design has effectively recreated the 1940s era, with vintage cars, costumes and old sign-boards that lend authenticity to the period setting.

As per the latest buzz, Benaras Mediaworks founder Anubhav Sinha , who is collaborating with Mishra for the second time after Afwaah (2023), shared further details. “Manoj has lost considerable weight for the movie and is currently in the ‘Gandhi zone’ on a restricted diet and a particular lifestyle. The movie’s shoot will continue till October in Lucknow. All we can share is that it’s about a 21-day chapter from Gandhi’s life. We just have a working title for now and we are working on a new title,” he says.

In further updates, Earlier, Mishra had elaborated on the movie’s unique narrative structure, stating, “It’s a movie within a movie, a dilemma of an star and Gandhi of that time and perception today. I started working on the script after she (mother) passed away as per the promise made to her. My mother told me many tales about Gandhi, and she was both fascinated and angry with him, as her father joined him in the independence struggle.”
On top of that, View this post on Instagram A post shared by Manoj Bajpayee (@bajpayee.manoj)

The 67-year-old filmmaker has shot multiple films in hometown Lucknow including Yeh Woh Manzil To Nahin (1987), Daas Dev (2018) and Afwaah besides his soon-to-release project tentatively titled Summers of 76 with actors Narendra Panjwani, Rajat Kapoor, Isha Talwar, Anoushka Pant and Saurabh Shukla.

title: Mirzapur The Movie box office day 2 (updated live): Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal film crosses ₹45 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window earnings day 2: Followers of the beloved series Mirzapur have been waiting for a long time for the spinoff. The movie opened to a grand start on Friday. The big-budget movie arrived with familiar characters and new faces, becoming the first major experiment of bringing an OTT IP to the big screens. Let us take a look at how the movie is performing so far.

Adding to this, Mirzapur: The Movie ticket-window earnings day 2: The movie features actors Ali Fazal, Divyendu Sharma, Pankaj Tripathi. (HT_PRINT) Mirzapur The Movie ticket-window update at 9 PM As per expectations, Mirzapur The Movie saw a bumper start on Friday, collecting ₹ 24.75 crore rupees on its opening day. For a movie which stars mainly character actors and not A-list stars, it is a huge number, showing how well the movie has been received for its reach with the beloved series. The collection even surpassed hits such as Saiyaara ( ₹ 22 crore rupees) and Awarapan 2 ( ₹ 21.50 crore rupees).

Meanwhile, On Saturday too, Mirzapur The Movie continued its dominance. According to Sacnilk, Mirzapur The Movie collected ₹ 31 crore rupees on its second day of rollout by 10 PM . The movie's biggest draw is from its Hindi version, collecting ₹ 30.75 crore rupees. The Telugu-dubbed version has not been really helpful, managing only ₹ 0.25 crore rupees. This brings total India gross collections to ₹ 68.20 crore rupees and total India net to ₹ 56.75 crore rupees .

Notably, Presented by Amazon MGM Studios and Excel Entertainment, Mirzapur: The Movie is directed by Gurmmeet Singh, written by Puneet Krishna and produced by Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar under the banner of Excel Entertainment. Kassim Jagmagia and Vishal Ramchandani serve as co-producers.

As per the latest buzz, Pankaj Tripathi is back as Kaleen Bhaiya, while Ali Fazal reprises his role as Guddu Pandit and Divyenndu returns as Munna Tripathi. Rasika Dugal and Harshita Gaur also return as Beena Tripathi and Dimpy Pandit, respectively. The ensemble features Shweta Tripathi, Abhishek Banerjee, Shriya Pilgaonkar, Sheeba Chadha, Rajesh Tailang, Sushant Singh and Mohit Malik, among others.

In further updates, An excerpt from the HT review read, "Divyenndu, as the hot-headed Munna, is clearly the crowd favourite, going by the cheers he received at my 9 AM show. It’s his most popular character to date, and he delivers big time. Next is Ali Fazal as the brawn-over-brains Guddu, and he is on point, too. Pankaj Tripathi as Kaleen Bhaiya is, as always, a delight. Rasika Dugal as Beena is the lone female character who actually helps drive the plot forward, and she does it well. Shriya Pilgaonkar and Shweta Tripathi don’t have much to do, but their presence in the Mirzapur world still feels nice. Kulbhushan Kharbanda, as the patriarch of the Tripathi family, also packs a punch. Ravi Kishan as Babban is formidable, and adds a lot of weight to the movie. Jitendra fits right in."

title: Sajid Nadiadwala's production house lease their office space in Mumbai's Andheri for a total rent of ₹2.46 crore
body: Here's the latest box office buzz making the rounds:

Sajid Nadiadwala’s production house, Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment Private Limited has leased commercial office units in Mumbai's Andheri West, to Rhea and Dia Enterprises Pvt Ltd. for a period of 28 months for a total rent of ₹ 2.46 crore rupees, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.

Adding to this, Sajid Nadiadwala’s production house, Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment Private Limited has leased commercial office units in Mumbai's Andheri West. (HT Files) The lease commenced on August 1, 2026, with the initial monthly rent for the two commercial office units set at ₹ 8.27 lakh. The transaction involves office premises located in Lotus Grandeur, a commercial building in Andheri West, according to property registration documents.

Meanwhile, According to the documents, the lease was registered on September 1, 2026, with the licence commencing on August 1, 2026. The company will pay a monthly licence fee of ₹ 8,26,875 for the office premises, while the security deposit for the transaction has been fixed at ₹ 30 lakh. The registered documents do not specify the area of the office premises.

Notably, The office premises, is situated on the eighth floor of Lotus Grandeur, also come with two car parking spaces. The property is situated in Andheri West, one of Mumbai's established commercial and residential real estate markets, with the Veera Desai Road area hosting a mix of corporate offices, production houses, creative businesses and residential developments.

As per the latest buzz, As per the terms of the agreement, the rent will increase by 5% every 12 months. Based on the agreed escalation, the monthly rent will rise to approximately ₹ 8.68 lakh from the 13th month and to around ₹ 9.12 lakh for the final four months of the 28-month tenure.
In further updates, The documents show that considering the escalation into account, the total rent payable over the entire 28-month lease period works out to approximately ₹ 2.46 crore rupees.
On top of that, The agreement also includes a lock-in period of 12 months, meaning the premises are subject to the agreed minimum occupancy commitment during the initial year of the lease.
Nadiadwala Grandson Entertainment Private Limited and Rhea and Dia Enterprises Pvt Ltd could not be reached for comment.

title: Amol Parashar asks audiences to ‘put our money where our mouth is’ for Mirzapur The Movie: ‘That’s how you bring change’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Amol Parashar has a message for audiences — go watch Mirzapur The Movie in theatres. Interestingly, the star has no part in the movie, but that did not stop him from rooting for its cast and the performers he believes deserve a larger theatrical audience. Through his social media posts, he shared that if audiences truly want better actors and stronger performances in mainstream cinema, they have to show their support at the ticket-window.

Adding to this, Want more talented actors on the big screen? Amol Parashar says, ‘Put our money where our mouth is’. Amol praises Mirzapur The Movie Amol Parashar began his post with a simple clarification, making sure there was no confusion about why he was backing the movie. “Go watch Mirzapur - The Movie in the theatres. No, I am not in the movie.” He shared his support comes from wanting audiences to show up for the actors who are actually part of the movie and have collected their place through years of work.

Meanwhile, Describing the cast as “some of the craftiest actors of our generation,” he pointed out that audiences have already seen their talent and know what they bring to the screen. “You've seen them at play; you've been entertained by their craft,” he wrote, underlining the bond these performers have built with viewers over the years.

Notably, He also drew attention to the journey behind that success, noting that these actors have had to work their way up and constantly prove themselves. “All of them are people who have built their careers from the ground up, years of leaving no stone unturned while simultaneously working on themselves,” he wrote. At the heart of his message was a simple request from the audience: “They want you to show up, to let them entertain you on the big screen.”

As per the latest buzz, View this post on Instagram A larger point about supporting talent Amol's message was not just about asking people to watch one movie. He used the post to make a larger point about the way audiences talk about mainstream cinema and the actors working in it. "While complaining about the quality of performances and performers in Indian mainstream cinema is a fun pastime for most of the country, here is a chance to put our money where our mouth is," he wrote.

In further updates, According to the star, liking an star or praising their work online is not enough. The strongest way for audiences to show their support is by actually buying a ticket and turning up for their films. “They know they are loved, no doubt. But business doesn't follow the love and respect you feel for your favourite actors; it follows the money you are willing to spend on them. That's how the audience makes itself heard,” he shared.

On top of that, He also feels that this can have a ripple effect on the industry. When audiences choose to support good performers at the ticket-window, it can encourage filmmakers and studios to give more opportunities to talented actors. “That's how you bring change in the business of cinema - when money follows talent, more talent follows my brothaa :).” For him, that would ultimately benefit everyone, which is why he ended his message on a hopeful note: “And that's a win for all of us :).”

Directed by Gurmeet Singh and penned by Puneet Krishna, Mirzapur: The Movie arrived in theatres on September 4, 2026, releasing in Hindi and with a Telugu-dubbed version. The movie takes the much-loved Prime Video franchise beyond streaming, bringing several of its most popular characters together for a larger, theatrical chapter.

title: Mahaprabhu Jagannath review: This devotional animated flick for kids is a one-time watch
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

After Mahavatar Narsimha (2024) comes yet another devotional animated movie, Mahaprabhu Jagannath. Content for children, designed to be experienced on the big screen, is anyway made so less. So it is always worthy of appreciation when films made for younger audiences get a proper theatrical rollout.

Adding to this, Mahaprabhu Jagannath review: A straightforward animated devotional movie for children. Plot of Mahaprabhu Jagannath However, if you walk into Mahaprabhu Jagannath expecting a detailed account of the deity’s life, you may be in for a disappointment. Director Shripad Warkhedkar and writer Pallavi Sharma instead build their story around the idea of Lord Jagannath being the best friend of a young boy. When villagers from the boy’s village begin mysteriously disappearing, he turns to his divine companion for help. How the Lord comes to their rescue forms the crux of the story.

Meanwhile, The beginning is shaky, as the movie takes some time to establish what its story is actually about. Much of the first half is spent establishing the bond between the Lord and the young boy. It clearly aims to educate children while making them curious to learn more about Indian history and mythology. However, its treatment, particularly the dialogues, isn't always accessible. The frequent use of religious jargon is likely to go over the heads of younger viewers, which ideally shouldn't be the case in a movie specifically designed to introduce children to these subjects.

Notably, The second half fares better, largely because there is finally some action to propel the narrative forward. The sequences are simple yet effective. The animation, however, is closer in scale and execution to what one would typically see in television cartoons and falls well short of what Indian animation demonstrated it is capable of with Mahavatar Narsimha. Even so, it remains decent and presentable. The music by Arijit Shrivastava is soothing and complements the mood of the movie well.

As per the latest buzz, Overall, Mahaprabhu Jagannath may not have the visual ambition or narrative finesse of some of the more accomplished animated films we have seen of late, but it does deserve credit for attempting to bring a story about Indian culture on the big screen. It works best when it keeps things simple and focuses on the warmth of the bond between its young protagonist and his divine companion. Its intentions are sincere, even if the execution leaves room for improvement. For younger viewers looking for a gentle introduction to Lord Jagannath , it could still prove to be a good watch.

body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

The Delhi Police on Saturday shared they arrested 21-year-old right-wing content creator Swatantra Bhardwaj , accused of severely injuring 38-year-old Sanjay Azad during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests at Jantar Mantar in Delhi in June over alleged irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET). The Patiala House court sent Bhardwaj to one day of police custody on Saturday.

Adding to this, Swatantra Bhardwaj, 21, and others are accused of assaulting Sanjay Azad, 38, who had gone to the protest with his daughter on June 23. (Instagram/ bhardwaj_swatantra_official) On June 23, Bhardwaj was booked for “voluntarily causing hurt” and wrongful restraint after Azad alleged that Bhardwaj and his aides attacked him, leaving him with more than seven stitches on his head.

Meanwhile, The June 23 first information report (FIR) shared Sanjay had accompanied his daughter to the protest when Bhardwaj and two to three others questioned him, asking, “Why are you making a video?”, after which an argument turned into a fight. Sanjay alleged that the men assaulted him.

Notably, On Wednesday, Bhardwaj appeared on a podcast where he claimed that he had “cracked the skull of Nishu’s (Azad’s daughter) father”. He also claimed that he did not go to jail and was let off because BJP leaders Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan were like his “elder brothers”.

As per the latest buzz, The podcast, uploaded on a YouTube channel, went widely shared, following which Azad’s 14-year-old daughter Nishu put out posts seeking help. The BHIM Army, CJP and the Indian Youth Congress staged a protest on Friday morning at the Parliament Street police station.
In further updates, A senior police officer verified to HT that the FIR has now been amended, with sections of the SC/ST Act and criminal intimidation added to the case.
On top of that, “In addition, a case under the POCSO Act has been lodged as the minor showed posts and messages from Bhardwaj and his associates who sent her rape threats,” shared the officer.
FIR was amended and Azad shared the Delhi Police assured them that action would be taken against Bhardwaj within 72 hours.

title: Teacher's Day 2026: Babil shares how Shoojit Sircar taught him to trust life
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Star Babil considers himself a lifelong student of acting, guided by two mentors: filmmaker Shoojit Sircar and acting coach Rachit Singh. On Teacher's Day, the young star explains the role these two mentors have had in shaping his mindset.

Adding to this, Babil pays tribute to Shoojit Sircar on this Teacher's Day “Shoojit da and I have been trying to work together for quite some time now. Even in that struggle to find the right subject and the right time, he taught me to trust life,” shares the 28-year-old.

Meanwhile, In learning to trust the process, Babil also discovered the importance of embracing the journey. “All this while, I was chasing outcomes when I should have been living the struggle itself for what it is, and developing my instinct through it while balancing that with rigorous practice of the craft,” he says.

Notably, These lessons, he believes, came from having the right teachers. “The difference between a good and a bad teacher can be whether the student lives their life or merely survives it,” says the star, who made his debut with Qala (2022) and is now preparing for his foray into Malayalam cinema.
As per the latest buzz, Shoojit Sircar says there was a lot of expectation from Babil since he is the late star Irrfan’s son.

In further updates, “But it’s wrong. He was just figuring out his way and the world was expecting him to deliver. That’s the worst scenario for anyone. I just tried to help him out of this trap. Whatever course correction he is doing, it’s purely his conviction for his art. He is still a student and we should give him that chance,” he insists, adding that Babil’s biggest strength is “his surety that he wanted to become an star”.

On top of that, Speaking about his other pillar of strength, Babil says, “Rachit sir and I have been working intricately on surrender and awareness for six years. His workshops changed my life and perspective, and showed me how to offer my throat to life and be fearless about it. The confidence I have today in my skills as an star and a human being stems largely from paaji’s workshops and friendship.”

Talking about an important moment with Rachit, Babil shares, “I think one moment that I can say without worrying is from paji’s workshops, especially the first one when I was trying to quit midway desperately afraid of failing and Rachit paji would call me incessantly and do whatever it takes which included literally dragging me out of bed and into the workshop to perform, I would usually perform well on these days but performing well wasn’t what he was trying to instil, it was confrontation with failure.”

title: Shalini Adnani on ''Our Share of Sand'': Wanted to explore society through a family''s story
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

New Delhi, In her India-set debut movie "Our Share of Sand", which is part of the Venice International Critics Week, director Shalini Adnani says she wanted to explore a society through the microcosm of a family with a young girl's perspective providing a window into the inequalities and exploitation that surround her.

Adding to this, Shalini Adnani on ''Our Share of Sand'': Wanted to explore society through a family''s story "Our Share of Sand", starring Maya Mehta, Mohammed Zeeshan Ayyub, Ellora Torchia, Krish Raj More and Jyoti Dogra, evolved from the many summers that Adnani, a Chilean-born, London-based filmmaker of Indian origin, spent in India.

Meanwhile, "I wanted to explore a society from the microcosm of a family... I think class and inequality in India is something that exists all the time, but we're not very aware of it. And it especially exists in our house as it's very much ingrained in the way that we live life day to day.

Notably, "I've always been interested in elements of class. I grew up in Latin America that also has quite a big class divide. It was just important for me to question. From a child's perspective, those things shouldn't really matter, but then suddenly, she's realising that we live in a society that puts a lot of value on that," Adnani told PTI in an interview.

As per the latest buzz, Recalling the time she spent in India as a child, when her grandmother would often take out her jewellery and ask her to choose something, Adnani shared she was interested in capturing the oral history that's passed down within families.

In further updates, "I didn't realise how important it is for women that it was this one thing that they had, where they essentially were protecting the family because things can happen, you have to maybe run away. And jewellery and diamonds were the one place where women felt like they could protect a family and that they had this value to add."

On top of that, The story of "Our Share of Sand", which was shot in Maharashtra, revolves around 12-year-old Maya who returns to India with her mother to reunite with her father, a sand mining business man. Immersed in a world where labour, legacy and extraction collide, she forms a fragile bond with Kiran, a young worker.
After a tragic accident, a police investigation turns Maya into a key witness, with her father relying on her testimony to save himself.

title: Ladakh Apex Body warns of bigger agitation ahead of talks with MHA on Sep 9
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Leh, Ahead of a sub-committee's meting on September 9 with the Ministry of Home Affairs in Delhi on September 9, the Leh Apex Body warned of an intensified agitation if the government fails to make "concrete" progress on its key demands.

Adding to this, Ladakh Apex Body warns of bigger agitation ahead of talks with MHA on Sep 9 The outfit has been demanding legislation for Ladakh at the Union Territory level, safeguards under Article 371, withdrawal of cases filed after the September 24 violence last year, compensation for victims, and publication of the inquiry commission report. LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance are jointly spearheading the agitation with the demands since the granting of UT status to Ladakh in August 2019 and have held several rounds of talks with the Centre since 2021.
Meanwhile, LAB chairman Chering Dorje Lakruk shared that though the group welcomes the meeting with MHA, it would assess the talks on the basis of their outcome.

Notably, "If the meeting produces a positive outcome... and if there is constructive and result-oriented dialogue on these issues, we will welcome it. Otherwise, we will intensify our agitation very strongly," he shared.

As per the latest buzz, Lakruk also expressed disappointment over the delay in the report of the inquiry commission constituted to investigate the September 24 incidents of last year that claimed four lives.

In further updates, He also questioned the pendency of cases against people booked in connection with the September 24 violence. Even as he welcomed the reported move to withdraw cases related to the July 20 Jantar Mantar incident in Delhi, he accused the Centre of "double standard" in the case of Ladakh.
On top of that, According to Lakruk, only 25 cases of the 80 related to last year's violence have so far been withdrawn.

"We are all Indians, and everyone should be treated equally. The lives of the people of Ladakh are not so cheap," he shared, demanding compensation for the kin of the dead and wounded in the agitation.

title: Tripura: Train services, vehicular movement hit as blockade by surrendered militants enters 2nd day
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Agartala, Train services and vehicular movement were affected in parts of Tripura on Saturday on the second day of a 72-hour blockade called by a forum of surrendered militants over an 11-point charter of demands, including the implementation of a tripartite agreement under which they laid down arms.

Adding to this, Tripura: Train services, vehicular movement hit as blockade by surrendered militants enters 2nd day Hundreds of surrendered militants under the banner of the All Returnees' Rehabilitation Committee blocked roads at Hataikotor, Brigudasbari and Khowai Chowmuhani in West Tripura district, a senior police officer shared.

Meanwhile, They also squatted on the railway tracks at Brigudasbari in West Tripura, prompting the Northeast Frontier Railway to announce short termination, cancellation and rescheduling of several trains, including long-distance trains, according to an official rollout.

Notably, Vehicular movement on the Assam-Agartala national highway, considered a lifeline in Tripura, was severely affected due to the blockade at Hataikotor, leaving the northeastern state completely isolated from the rest of the country.

As per the latest buzz, The All Returnees' Rehabilitation Committee, representing seven surrendered militant groups, started the 72-hour blockade on Friday, on the 11-point charter of demands, including implementation of the peace accord signed in 2024, under which they laid down arms before Chief Minister Manik Saha.

In further updates, "We had a discussion with former rebel leaders at Hataikotor on various points of the peace accord. They have raised some demands to which the government is ready to work. The government is committed to implementing the accord in a time-bound manner," West Tripura District Magistrate Vishal Kumar told reporters after the meeting on Friday.
On top of that, He shared the former rebel leaders shared they would deliberate on the government's proposals with the cadres and would communicate to the administration as soon as possible.
The 11-point charter of demands includes land rights for the indigenous people and withdrawal of all pending cases against the surrendered militants.

title: Vijay Subramaniam on AI, Indian mythology and why Hanuman can rival Marvel: ‘His gada is greater than Thor’s hammer’
body: Here's the latest update from the Hollywood/Marvel world:

For Vijay Subramaniam , Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not meant to replace the people who tell stories. He sees it as another tool that can help filmmakers think bigger, work faster and take on stories that may otherwise be difficult to produce. As Group CEO of Collective Artists Network, Subramaniam has built the company around talent, creators and content, while also exploring newer ways of making and distributing entertainment. He of late produced Musafir Cafe , starring Vikrant Massey , Vedika Pinto and Mahima Makwana. His latest focus is on using technology to bring Indian stories, particularly those rooted in mythology and history, to a wider audience.

Adding to this, ‘Hanuman’s gada is greater than Thor’s hammer’: Vijay Subramaniam on AI and taking Indian mythology global. Projects such as Mahabharat and Chiranjeevi Hanuman are part of that vision. But Vijay's argument goes beyond the technology itself. In a conversation with Hindustan Times, Vijay discusses AI, the future of creative jobs, India's rich mythology, reaching younger audiences and his plans for Collective Artists Network.

Meanwhile, Vijay looks at AI as the latest step in a long line of technological changes that have shaped filmmaking. He draws a comparison with animation, VFX and Unreal Engine, all of which have expanded what filmmakers can create while making large-scale production more achievable.

Notably, He says, “A lot is made of this word AI. What people need to understand is that when Unreal Engine came in, when VFX was invented, when animation techniques came in, it basically brought down the cost of production and helped you tell stories at a grander level. It's as simple as that. I look at AI as a tool. If you ask me what is changing, nothing changes from the first principles of filmmaking. There are writers, directors, production designers, costume designers, DOPs and all your HODs. Those people will remain in an animated movie or a live-action movie. You have to be good at your job even in a movie that is backed by technology."

As per the latest buzz, He adds, "Today, of course, we are working with hybrid pipelines. Are we doing everything on AI? No. We are also using a lot of 3D and VFX, and running them through AI pipelines. But from motion capture to image transfer to emotion transfer, we are able to do it at scale simply because it is affordable. Otherwise, if I have to make Mahabharat, be true to Mahabharat and make it like Game of Thrones, it's going to cost me more than ₹ 1,000 crore rupees and take me seven or eight years to make. So, for me, the pivot was very simple. I wanted to tell stories of India. I wanted to tell stories of Indian history, and I wanted to tell them at scale.”

In further updates, AI's impact on jobs has become one of the biggest concerns around the technology, particularly in creative industries where animation, VFX, illustration and design are all increasingly using AI tools. Vijay, however, does not believe this necessarily means that creative professionals will be pushed out. He points to the people already working on his projects and says the technology is being used to support their work rather than replace them.

On top of that, He asserts, “I have engineers who are doing work in creative fields. I have VFX supervisors, sketch artists, storyboard artists — they're all part of the production. There is so much hype about this. Maybe it's true in other jobs where AI is taking jobs, but in the creative field, it's only enhancing creativity. I have three National Award-winning directors making films. So, for me, that is not really a problem. I think people are overhyping this idea that AI will take your job away in the creative field.”

The concern, however, is not limited to filmmaking. Across media, there is already a shift towards expecting one person to take on multiple responsibilities, with technology making it easier to write, edit, research and produce content. Vijay sees this as part of a much larger pattern of change rather than something unique to AI. He says, “But how is that different from any evolution? It is as debatable as any other industrial revolution in history. You've had lakhs and lakhs of postmen all around the world. Then email happened. What do you do then? Back in the day, before the internal combustion engine was invented, you had chariot riders. Then you got from Point A to Point B faster. Today, you have Pepsi being delivered to your house in 10 minutes without going to the kirana store. Technology advancement always comes at the cost of some incumbency. You can't just look at it from field to field. You have to look at it as universal technology. The internet didn't disrupt one sector. It disrupted all sectors. So, I don't know why there is so much noise around this."

title: Swatantra Bhardwaj detained after big CJP protest, POCSO case filed after ‘rape threats’ to minor
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Delhi Police on Friday detained a 21-year-old right-wing content creator accused of severely injuring a 38-year-old man during the Jantar Mantar protests in June, officers shared, hours after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other politicians staged a massive protest at the Parliament Street police station.

Adding to this, Swatantra Bhardwaj describes himself as a “Swatantra Sanatani Yodha” on his profile. (Instagram/ bhardwaj_swatantra_official) The accused, identified as Swatantra Bhardwaj, 21, and others allegedly attacked a man named Sanjay Azad, 38, who had accompanied his 14-year-old daughter to the protest on June 23.

Meanwhile, Azad, a Dalit person, suffered severe injuries to his head but an FIR was lodged the same day at Parliament Street police station only under BNS sections 115(2) (causing simple hurt) and 126(2) (wrongful restraint). Bhardwaj was briefly detained the same day but was rolled out hours later, and later claimed on social media that he was friends with top politicians — he mentioned the names of Union minister Chirag Paswan and Delhi minister Kapil Mishra — of the ruling establishment.

Notably, “Finally, Delhi Police have registered an FIR against the Sanghi goon and shared he will be arrested within 72 hours. It took two months and a protest just to get an FIR registered for a hate crime that happened right in front of the police!” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared in a post on X.

As per the latest buzz, After the protest, police also added sections under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Union minister Paswan distanced himself from Bhardwaj.

In further updates, Another FIR has been lodged under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and sections of the BNS, police shared after a complaint was filed regarding the minor receiving rape threats from Bhardwaj.

On top of that, While Delhi Police and Bulandshahr police refused to give details about the detention, investigating officials, who spoke to HT and did not wish to be named, shared a team was sent to Bulandshahr late on Friday afternoon. Bhardwaj was held after his phone location was traced, shared a police officer. Police are yet to obtain his transit remand as of late Friday evening.
Delhi minister Mishra did not issue a statement on Bhardwaj’s claims.

title: Taapsee Pannu questions Bollywood’s ‘same actors’ formula: ‘All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same’ | Interview
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

Taapsee Pannu has often spoken about how an star can get boxed into a certain image once audiences and filmmakers associate them with a particular kind of role. After years of playing strong, intense characters, she feels that perception can sometimes be a limitation. In a recent chat with Hindustan Times, the star spoke about Gandhari , the creative bankruptcy in Bollywood and why the industry only offers her certain kinds of roles.

Adding to this, Taapsee Pannu says Bollywood films look the same: ‘There are only those four or five actors’. What Gandhari gave her For Taapsee, the conversation around casting is not limited to the kind of stories actors are offered. She feels that an star’s appearance can also shape how filmmakers picture them in a role. “When it comes to certain visuals of a character, it's a lot to do with vanity more than how that star is born and looks,” she says.

Meanwhile, Gandhari gave Taapsee a chance to break away from that image. She plays Bani, a mother desperately searching for her kidnapped daughter, and her journey takes her into the unsettling world of Joypurra, where she uncovers a series of disturbing truths.

Notably, A big part of her transformation stemmed from how Bani was visually created. Taapsee credits her hair, makeup and costume teams for helping her look completely different from her usual self. “I would like to take the credit, not just myself, but with my look-creating people — the hair, makeup, costume — to be able to make me look like Bani in this movie, because I'm nowhere close to her in real life, how I look,” she adds. “Even on my worst stress days, I will not look like that.”

As per the latest buzz, That, she feels, is how an star should approach a character. You do not necessarily have to look like the person you are playing in real life. Sometimes it is the story and world of the movie that determine what the character should look like. “It’s the character and the world that demanded me to look like that,” she says.

In further updates, Taapsee also believes that Bollywood 's casting choices play a role in why so many films today end up feeling similar. She feels that filmmakers often return to the same actors for similar stories, leaving little room for a fresh combination of star and character. If the industry wants its films to feel different, she believes the casting needs to change, too.

On top of that, “All the rom-coms, glam stuff looks the same because there are only those four or five actors, actresses who are doing that. All our thrillers look and feel the same because there are only those four or five actors who are doing that,” she says. “If you really want your movie to look different, something new, something different, then you need to cast people who can bring that difference on screen.”

For Taapsee, putting a familiar star in a different outfit or changing their styling does not necessarily make the character feel new. The audience already has a certain image of an star, and that stays with them even when the appearance changes. “If I've seen someone in a glamorous role, now you make that person wear a sari or a bikini or whatever, I have seen the glamour of that star. It's only different, right?” she adds. “So that's not the fault of that poor star, also.”

title: Hanuman Ansh director Vishal Chaturvedi recalls OTT rejection as film crosses ₹80 cr mark: ‘It was derogatory’
body: Here's the latest on what's streaming and coming up:

Vishal Chaturvedi's directorial Hanuman Ansh has worked a miracle of sorts at the ticket-window. The movie, which no one was talking about until a while ago, picked up pace at the ticket-window , so much so that it has now crossed the ₹ 80 crore rupees mark. While many are celebrating the movie's success today, its director opened up that he faced rejection when he pitched the movie to an OTT platform.

Adding to this, Vishal Chaturvedi spoke about Hanuman Ansh. 'The language they used was derogatory' In conversation with India TV, he recalled, “I had gone to pitch my story on an OTT platform, and there they told me that I have an Indian story with international relevance. I narrated Maharaj Ji’s story in such a way that I literally broke down."

Meanwhile, Vishal recalled that the platform rejected his movie, but he found the manner in which they did so derogatory and insulting. He also shared that as a filmmaker he is used to rejections but there is a way to reject someone's project.

Notably, He shared, "Mujhe laga jis tarah unhone reject kiya, jis bhaasha ka prayog kiya, woh thodi derogatory thi (The way they rejected, the language they used to reject me was derogatory). The way they shared it, I felt that the narrative in their mind, the way they rejected it, there is a hole in their mind through the narrative. Now it is necessary to bust that narrative. We are filmmakers, we have been rejected a thousand times. You narrate a story and if you don’t understand it, you say that it is good, but we will do it later."

As per the latest buzz, Hanuman Ansh, which rolled out in theatres on August 7, had a slow start at the ticket-window, earning merely ₹ 10 lakh on its opening day. The movie collected around ₹ 1.80 crore rupees in its first week of rollout and just ₹ 40 lakh in its second week.

In further updates, However, the movie witnessed a major turnaround in its third week, driven by strong word of mouth. Footfalls began increasing steadily, with shows eventually turning into house-full screenings. The movie saw a tremendous rise in its collections, minting ₹ 10.40 crore rupees in its third week. Its box-office momentum continued into the fourth week, when it collected ₹ 61 crore rupees. The movie's India gross collection now stands at ₹ 96.03 crore rupees, while its total India net collection has reached ₹ 81.41 crore rupees.

On top of that, The devotional drama Hanuman Ansh is based on the life of spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba. The movie is written, directed and produced by Dr Vishal Chaturvedi, and stars Shobhinaw Satyaa in the lead role.

title: ‘Very distressing’: SC judge says ‘dismayed’ to see police personnel assault Jantar Mantar protesters
body: Here's the latest protest news from across India:

Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan shared on Friday that seeing police personnel assault students and other protesters at Jantar Mantar in July was "distressing" and "a matter of grave concern".

Adding to this, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan made the remarks at the launch of "Policing the Republic", a book by former secretary (security) Yashovardhan Azad. (Screengrab from PTI video/ANI) His comments came days after he shared students must not face punitive action for expressing a different opinion or asking questions.

Meanwhile, Justice Bhuyan as per reports made the remarks at the launch of "Policing the Republic", a book by former secretary (security) Yashovardhan Azad. The event took place at Viceroy Hall in the national capital.

Notably, "All of us are dismayed when we see young officers of the Indian Police Service personally going and assaulting protesters and demonstrators. This is something very, very distressing to observe," he was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.
As per the latest buzz, "The detachment expected of police officers somehow seems to be disappearing, and this is indeed a matter of grave concern," he added.

In further updates, "For most common people, a policeman on the street wearing a whistle and a lathi represents the power and authority of the state. When they feel wronged, they seek the help of the police. It is, therefore, of utmost importance that the police force maintains its credibility," he shared.

On top of that, "It can do so only by strictly adhering to the Constitution, by functioning as a truly professional force, acting impartially, displaying courage and acting with conviction, maintaining integrity and adhering to secular principles, thereby upholding the rule of law," he added.
He also raised concerns over the growing number of cases involving custodial torture and deaths in the country, calling it one of the worst crimes in a civilised society.

title: Abhishek Pathak, Sandeep Francis’ Switch Off selected for L’Étrange Festival in Paris
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:
Abhishek Pathak and Sandeep Francis’ 11-minute thriller Switch Off has been selected for the 32nd L’Étrange Festival in Paris.

Adding to this, The selection comes after the short movie was also screened at South Korea’s Bucheon International Fantastic Movie Festival (BIFAN). Pathak, who has produced the movie, shared the Paris selection offers a different kind of recognition for the project.
Meanwhile, “Being selected for L’Étrange Festival Paris is a wonderful recognition for the movie and the team,” Pathak shared.
Notably, Abhishek Pathak on the movie’s international run

As per the latest buzz, Switch Off follows a mobile repairman whose night takes an unexpected turn after he finds himself alone on the streets of Kochi. Pathak shared he was drawn to the way Francis approached the story and built its atmosphere.

In further updates, “What attracted me was the way Sandeep had approached the story. The movie largely takes place at night, beginning inside a small mobile repair shop where the repairman is working alone. From there, he finds himself alone on the streets of Kochi,” he shared.

On top of that, Pathak believes the movie’s narrative style could connect with festival audiences in Paris. “I think they will connect with the way the story is told. The movie gets the audience into the world very quickly and keeps the story moving,” he shared.

He also spoke about the difference between commercial success and festival recognition. “They are very different experiences. A box-office success gives you the excitement of scale, while a festival selection gives you the satisfaction of seeing a story travel in a completely different environment. For us, having Switch Off selected at L’Étrange Festival Paris is a very special moment,” Pathak shared.

title: Aamir Khan admits feeling ‘hurt’ after Reema Kagti scolded him on Lagaan sets: ‘I'm the producer’
body: Here's the latest update from the Bollywood world:

On the occasion of his movie Dil Chahta Hai turning 25, Aamir Khan and the movie's cast and crew sat together to share their memories of the movie. Meanwhile, Aamir also recalled the times he was scolded by filmmaker Reema Kagti for arriving late on the sets of Talaash and Lagaan.

Adding to this, Aamir Khan in Lagaan. 'How dare you come late?' In conversation with We Are Yuvaa, Aamir shared that during Talaash, which Reema was directing, he had asked her if he could arrive one hour late on set as he wanted to attend former cricketer Sachin Tendulkar's retirement party. However, the party ran late, and Aamir arrived almost 4-5 hours late. Aamir shared, “I thought, ‘Aaj Reema se daant kha lenge (Today I will accept scolding from Reea ). Sachin Tendulkar ke liye itna bhi chalega’ (Will accept this for Sachin). She blasted me.. she shared, ‘How dare you come late? Is this your professionalism?’ Itna mujhe sunaya. I am still working on her (anger). We are getting there.”

Meanwhile, This wasn't the first time Reema scolded Aamir. They had previously worked together on Lagaan, in which Aamir played the main lead and also served as the producer of the movie. Reema, on the other hand, was the second assistant director on the movie.

Notably, While speaking during the interview, Aamir recalled how he had requested Reema to call him 15 minutes before the other cast and crew for breakfast, as he takes time to have his food. Reema, on the other hand, refused Aamir's request and decided not to make an exception for him. She told him that his hair and makeup team would not come 15 minutes before the others either.

As per the latest buzz, Admitting that he was hurt by Reema's remark, he shared, "I'm the producer, and she is scolding me. I shared, 'It takes time for me.' She shared, 'I don't care; you have to come.' She spoke to me very harshly. I felt hurt. It didn't affect her; she shared, 'Very good, you can be read on time then.' After a week, exhausted, I went back to having breakfast there again."
